    1. General Information

        Field Introduction

     Azadegan South Oil  Field  is  situated  in West Karoun province on a  large  long-axis
       anticline with N-S trending with approximate dimensions about 20 km width and 60
    km length near to Iran-Iraq border, to the east of Yaran Oil Field.

     The  trap area of the south Azadegan  is  limited  to 43.2x17.2 km. The Azadegan  Oil
       field was discovered  in 1999, when Well AZN-1 was  drilled  vertically down  to  the
      Cretaceous Fahliyan Formation with  total depth  of 4,643m. The  results  of  this  well,
      revealed the  reservoir  characteristics of the  field. Following  to the  result of the well
      no. AZN-1,  another 5  exploration  wells was  drilled  in  different  parts  of  this huge
       field down  to  Fahliyan  Formation.  In  the  later  stage  the  well  No.10  assumed  as
      exploration well  for  evaluation  of deeper  formations. This well was  drilled  in 2008,
     down to the depth of 5340m (Neyriz Fm.), mainly to evaluate the Jurassic formations.

     Based on  the  exploration  wells  results,  carbonate  reservoir  of  Sarvak  Formation  is
      broadly developed  in Azadegan  Field. This formation was  penetrated  in  all of seven
      exploration  wells  (AZN-1,  AZN-2,  AZN-3,  AZN-4,  AZN-5, AZN-6  and  AZN-10).
      Clastic  oil-bearing  zones  of  Kazhdumi  Formation  developed  in  main  anticline  of
     Azadegan  Field, extending from north  to  center of South Azadegan. The  Clastic  oil-
      bearing zones of Gadvan Formation developed only  in  crest area and south  parts  of
     South Azadegan Filed, which was discovered by AZN-1 in crest and AZN-4 in south
       parts. The  carbonates  of  Fahliyan  Formation  also  developed  in Azadegan  field,  but
      the oil reservoir of this formation developed in South part of South Azadegan.

     The Azadegan Field  is an elongated  anticline, trending in N-S direction, belonging to
      "Arabian Trend".

     The  stratigraphy  sequence  of  the   field  includes  AghaJari,  Gachsaran,  Fahliyan,
      Pabdeh,  Gurpi,  Ilam,  Laffan,  Sarvak,  Kazhdumi,  Dariyan,  Gadvan  and  Fahliyan
      Formations, from top to bottom. This sequence in well no AZN-10, the deepest up to
    now  drilled well  of  the  field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah,  Sargalu, Alan,
    Mus and Neyriz formations.

     The  Dominant  lithofacies  of  Sarvak  Formation  are  Rudist-bearing  packstone  and
       partially  grainstone,  which  contains  abundant   bioclasts.  Some  other   facies   like
      matrix-dominated wackestone and mudstone are also found.

     The AZADEGAN  Oilfield  is  Located  in  Khuzestan  Province  and  is  Approximately
      Located 80 Kilometers West  of Ahwaz  City,  near  to  Iran-Iraq  Border.  It  is  in The
      Northwest  of The YADAVARAN  Field  and  in The West  of JUFEYR  Field. The
     Average Monthly Temperature  is 45ºc  in summer, and Highest Temperature  is  52ºc.
     The  Lowest  Temperature   is  -4.4ºc  in  winter. Maximum  Rainfall   is  78 mm  in
      February, Winter Season.

     Fahliyan  Formation:  This  carbonate  to  argillaceous  carbonate  Formation   is
      limited  by   overlying   thick   argillaceous  successions   in   the  upper   part
      (eaquivalent  to  the  Iraqi  Ratawi  Formation)  and  the  main  part  consists  of
      different  bioclastic  limestones  with  some  layers  of  shale  and  argillaceous
      facies   that  can  be  assumed  equivalent   with   Iraqi  Yamama  Formation.
     However,  in  South Azadegan  wells  1, 2 and 5  the  Fahliyan  Formation  is
      characterized  by   fossiliferous  limestone  beds  and  interbedded  shales.    It
     should be noted  that most  of Majnoon  wells penetrated  into the Sarvak and
     Fahliyan carbonates as one of the main reservoir targets.

    The AZNS-040 well was drilled from 26-Mar-2014 to 10-May-2014 by CNPCI to total
     depth 1493m and suspended. Drilling and well suspend sequences are describe in the
      following.

         26” Hole Section Summary

     This section was drilled from 15 to 153 m using one rock bit (26" Simth, Type:
    MSDGH, IADC 135) and bentonite mud w/ 65.5-71.8 pcf weight. Performed ream
     and back ream prior to each connection. When TD was reached, wiper trip and
    CBU to clean the hole were done with good condition. Spotted Hi-Vis  pill at
     bottom, dropped single shot to take a survey that resulted in 0.2° at 150 m. 20ʺ
    CSG (K-55, 117 ppf, Big Omega) was run to 152.5 m and cemented in place by
      stinger with 346 bbls cement class G, 117 pcf. 50 bbls slurry returned to surface.
    N/U 20 3⁄4ʺ CHH 3K on 20ʺ CGS supported by a base plate and performed
     pressure test by 400 psi, 15min. N/U 20 3⁄4ʺ BOP 3K and performed pressure
       test. 17 1⁄2ʺ milled tooth bit was RIH, tagged TOC at 150.5 m, 20ʺ CGS pressure
      tested with 1650 psi /15min, then D/O cement & shoe.
      Total Duration for this section was 4 days and 2 hrs. until new formation of next
      section was started to drill.

          17-1/2” Hole Section Summary

      Drilled 17 1⁄2" hole section from 153m to 1493m, MW: 71.8-85.5pcf NaCl-KCl polymer
    Mud &Saturated NaCl Polymer Mud. LOT@156m with 80psi, MW: 71.1pcf, EMD:
     93.64 pcf. Took survey and wiper trip every 200m to ensure good well track and hole
      condition, try to control viscosity and water loss of mud as program, due to claystone
    & gypsum exist in the interval. From the depth of 1159m to 1385m, we meet very low
    ROP (min-ROP is 0.1 m/h). total used 5pcs of bits (1 used rock bit, 3 used PDC bits
     and 1 new PDC bit) when during drilling 17-1/2" hole. total footage 1340m, actual
       drilling time 687.3Hrs, ROP: 1.95 m/h.

     Performed condition hole before run wireline logging (Items: GR, CDR, CALI). After
      logging performed 1 more time hole condition prior to run casing, Spotted high
      viscosity mud pill at bottom of the hole.
    Ran 13 3/8” CSG (68ppf-N80- BTC) to 1492m (casing shoe).

     Performed cementing job: Cement track pumped 25m3 spacer (1.05sg) with FR
     317gpm, SPP 200-478psi, dropped BTM plug, pumped 2m3 of spacer(1.05sg), follow
     by 147.0m3 of lead slurry(average 1.45sg, Max 1.51sg, Min 1.45sg ) with FR 528gpm,
    SPP 1015-345psi, pumped 48m3 tail slurry (average 1.85sg, Max 1.89sg, Min 1.83sg)

      surface. WOC, While L/D 5"DPS.

    R/D 13-5/8"*10K BOP single ram. Cover the wellhead with steel plate, and fixed with 4
     pieces of bolts and suspend the well
      Total Duration for this section was 41 days and 7 hrs. until release the rig.

      AZNS-040 Re-Entry Well Program Outline

     AZNS-40 well, was planned to be drilled as Horizontal well in Sarvak formation on Pad-
      50. The well was drilled by CNPCI to total depth 1493m in Gachsaran formation as 17-
      1/2” hole section, 13-3/8” CSG ran and cemented to surface and well has been suspended
     by CMT plug.

     As the Previous exploration/delineation drilling in Azadegan oilfield has proved presence
      of a very prolific hydrocarbon bearing sedimentary column, particularly within the
      Cretaceous sequences. The Fahliyan Formation was divided into 6 zones, named as
      Fahliyan top, Fah-1, Fah-2, Fah-3, Fah-4 and Fah-5.

     The objective of Re-Entry this well is to De-suspend the well, vertical drilling 12-1/4″ &
      8-1/2″ hole section to new well target in Fahliyan reservoir (Well target has been
     changed from Sarvak horizontal well to Fahliyan vertical well), run 9-5/8” CSG and
     7” Liner, perforate 7” Liner in Fahliyan formation and complete the well as Fahliyan
       vertical oil producer well.

     The AZNS-040 Re-Entry sequences summarize as follow:

                                                                                    Page 16 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                 AZNS-040 Re-Entry ProgramContract No:
                                                                                         Page 17 of 205053-073-9125        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

     De-Suspend the Well:

     Monitor wellhead pressure and make sure about wellhead integrity. Remove wellhead cover,
    N/U BOPs. P/U & M/U 12-1/4” D/Out BHA, RIH to top of CMT plug @ 55m, D/Out CMT plug
        f/ 55-100m with water, RIH to top of 13-3/8” CSG Float collar, D/Out shoe track to 3m above
      shoe with water, displace well with 75 pcf Salt Saturated/Polymer mud, perform 13-3/8” CIT,
     D/Out shoe track to 1493m.

     12-¼" Hole Section:

       Drill 12-1/4” vertical hole section f/ 1493m to 3986m through Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam,
      Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan formations with 75-87 pcf Salt
      Saturated KCL/Glycol/Polymer mud. Then Full Suite/CDR/GR Logs will be run. The 9-5/8”
      Casing will be set at  3986m and it will be cemented in one stage as primary cementing up to
       surface. N/U13-5/8”, 5K x 11”, 10K THS and then N/U 13-5/8”, 10K BOPs. RIH with D/Out
    BHA to TOC, D/Out to 7m above shoe, perform 9-5/8” CIT. Run D/Out 9-5/8” Cement quality
       log. RIH with 8-1/2” PDC Bit BHA to 7m above shoe, D/Out shoe track to 3986m while displace
      well with 100 pcf Salt Saturated Kcl/Polymer/CaCo3 mud.

     8-½" Hole Section:

     The 8-½" hole section will be drilled vertically from 3986m to 4200m in Fahliyan formation
      with 100-106 pcf Salt Saturated Kcl/Polymer/CaCo3 mud. Then Full Suite/CDR/GR Logs will
     be carried out over 8-½" open hole section to evaluate Fahliyan reservoir. The 7” Liner will be
      run and set at ± 4200m and it will be cemented in one stage as primary cementing up to  7
      Stands Wet above Liner Lap. Clean out to 7” L.Lap and inside 7” liner to LDC. Perform 7” Liner
      CIT, L.Lap positive and negative tests and run 7” Liner Cement quality Log. Displace 7” Liner
     volume with CaBr2 perforation fluid, perform 7” Liner perforation, run CCL/GR log to confirm
      perforated interval. RIH with 5-7/8” Bit to top of perforation while scrap 7” production PKR
       setting depth, displace well volume with CaBr2 completion fluid. Run 4-1/2" * 3-1/2", 10K
     Completion string. N/D BOP, N/U XMT. Perform well Pre-Acid clean up, Acid-Wash, Post-
     Acid clean up and well performance test operations. Secure the well and release the Rig.

      2. Geological Information

         Structural Geology

       The Azadegan  oil field  is located at 80km west of Ahwaz  is an elongated
          anticline,  trending  in N-S  direction,  belongs  to  Arabian Trend  which  is
          different  from  “Zagros  Trend”.  There   is  no  outcrop   for  Azadegan
         structure and   it was detected by 2D seismic  interpretation. The Previous
         exploration/delineation  drilling  in Azadegan  oil  field has proved presence
         of  a  very  prolific  hydrocarbon  bearing  sedimentary  column,  particularly
         within  the  Cretaceous  sequences.  Fahliyan  Formation   is  one  of  the
        important hydrocarbon  reservoirs  in the southern  part  of Azadegan  field,
        which has been developed  in recent years. The Fahliyan Formation was
         divided  into 6 zones, named as Fahliyan  top, Fah-1, Fah-2, Fah-3, Fah-
       4 and Fah-5.

          Figure 2-1: Distribution of Fahliyan wells in South Azadegan Oilfield on Top of Fah-1 Zone

        Formation Description

       The stratigraphy sequence of this field includes Aghajari, Gachsaran, Asmari,
       Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi, Dariyan, Gadvan and Fahliyan
         formations. This sequence in well no. AZN-10, the deepest up to now drilled well
         of the field, continues with Garau, Gotnia, Najmah, Sargalu, Alan, Mus and Neyriz
         formations.

       The AZN-040 Re-Entry well is carried out inside of Gachsaran to Fahliyan
        Formations, a brief stratigraphic description of these formations in South
       Azadegan field has been described as follows:

            Gachsaran Formation
        This formation begins with white, glassy, soft, medium, hard anhydrite and off
         white, light gray to gray, soft to medium hard, dolomitic limestone. Comprises of
        anhydrite interbedded with gray marl and red marl, salt beds of variable thickness
       and some thin limestone beds. This formation in type section not divided to other
       member. The Anhydrite is white off white, milky, soft, and partly crystalline to
          crystalline, medium hard to hard. The Gray marl is gray to light gray, soft. The
      Red marl is red brown to brown, soft, sticky. The Limestone is gray to light gray,
         buff to buff gray, hard, and slightly dolomitic.
            Asmari Formation
       The Asmari Formation in Azadegan Field developed a massive sandstone
          interval, with a few thin argillaceous limestones in the upper sections. Sandstone
        are clear, fine to medium-sorted, and poorly consolidated. On the other hand,
        the lower sections consist of intercalation of sandy, chalky, slightly dolomitic
        high-energy limestone with sandstone layers.
            Pabdeh Formation
       Pabdeh Formation is divided into two parts in the Azadegan field. The upper part
           is made of grey to dark- brown argillaceous limestone and marl. Planktonic
        fauna dates that this part was deposited in Oligocene. The lower part is
       composed of dark-brown, slightly argillaceous limestone. Pelagic fauna, mostly
        Globigerina and Globorotalia, indicates that this part was formed during late
       Paleocene to late Eocene in age. It seems that no early Paleocene formation
         exists in the Azadegan area.
            Gurpi Formation
        This formation consists of three main units: a) Upper Gurpi Member b) Tarbour
       Tongue c) Lower Gurpi Member.
            Upper Gurpi Member
        This member begins with light gray, gray, off white, soft to medium, sticky
         argillaceous limestone. The Upper Gurpi Member is mostly consisting of gray
         buff to gray with of trace partly buff gray, dark gray, medium hard to hard
         argillaceous, high argillaceous graded to marl argillaceous limestone
        interbedded with anhydrite marl and chalky limestone beds. The anhydritic marl
           is light gray to gray, soft, sticky, graded to high argillaceous calcareous. The
        chalky limestone is light gray to buff gray, medium hard to soft, chalky. II, a
          slightly argillaceous.
             Tarbur Tongue
         In the western Abadan Plain about 50 meters thick chalky limestone was
        encountered in the middle part of the Gurpi Formation, which contains abundant
        fragments of bioclasts, suggesting very shallow depositional environment. This

                                                                                 Page 30 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                 AZNS-040 Re-Entry ProgramContract No:

               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

          interval is equivalnt to the Tarbur Formation with reservoir quality in other
         regions.
            Lower Gurpi Member
        This Member begins with off white, cream, soft to medium hard argillaceous
        limestone and light gray to gray, soft, sticky marl. The Member consisting of dark
        gray to gray, light gray, soft to medium hard argillaceous limestone and light
       cream and soft. II, A. chalky limestone beds.
             Ilam Formation
        This formation is mostly consisting of limestone interbedded with shale and clay
        stone beds. The Limestone is cream, buff to buff gray, light brown, soft to
       medium hard, chalky, II, A, oil stained Partly slightly argillaceous. The Shale is
        green gray to light green gray, mostly brown gray, medium hard, pyritic, slightly
        calcareous. The Claystone is green gray to light green gray and soft, slightly
        calcareous.
             Laffan Formation
       The Laffan Formation is mostly consists of greenish-grey pyritic shale layer with
        ostracods fauna interbedded with Claystone beds that capping the Sarvak
        Formation.
            Sarvak Formation
       The Sarvak Formation developed a carbonate unit, which was gradually
         overlying the Kazhdumi Formation, and it is abruptly terminated by an erosion
        phase, covered by a various late Cretaceous sediment. The lithology of Sarvak
         consists of the dark grey fine grained nodular argillaceous limestone
        interbedded with thin marls in the bottom. The Limestone graded upward into a
         white-to-buff massive chalky limestone with siliceous nodules; developed a very
       massive tan-to-brown limestone containing abundant rudist debris in the middle
          part. In the upper part is made up of rubbly limestone with red staining and
        leached zones of breccia and the top of Sarvak Formation is very ferruginous.
        For the layering scheme of the reservoir section, sequence stratigraphic concept
       was applied to the Azadegan wells. Judging from the characteristics of gamma
        ray and other wireline logs, relative sea- level change during the deposition of
        the reservoir sections were interpreted in terms of sequence stratigraphic
         context. Based upon the sea-level change inferred, the sections were
         interpreted as vertical accumulation of a number of zones, each of which is
         geologically termed as a depositional sequence, implicitly representing a
         genetically related body of sedimentary sequence. The formation was divided
          totally into thirteen zones by interpreting.
            Kazhdumi Formation
        This formation is start with dark brown to dark green gray, medium hard to hard,
          soft to medium, high Bituminous, calcareous shale interbedded with argillaceous
        limestone, sandy claystone, claystone, marl, sandy limestone, limestone beds.
        the middle part developed light-grey, micritic to chalky limestone, the low part, is
       around 40-60m in thichness clean channel sands interbeded with argillaceous
       sands with streaks of shale.

                                                                                 Page 31 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                 AZNS-040 Re-Entry ProgramContract No:
                                                                                         Page 32 of 205053-073-9125        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

            Dariyan Formation
         In the Azadegan Field, the average thickness of the Dariyan Formation is 183.5
       m; its greatest thickness is 197.5 m in well AZN-1. This formation overlies the
       Gadvan Formation conformably and is overlain disconformably by the Kazhdumi
        Formation. Dariyan Formation starts with white to white cream grey clean
        limestone type I/II, I. Base of Dariyan Formation appears grey, green pyritic
        shale interbedded with argillaceous limestone. This zone called transition zone
       and thickness is 16m. after last grey limestone indicates of Gadvan Formation.
            Gadvan Formation
         In this formation a variety of lithological rock types such as carbonates, rich
        organic shales and sandstones were deposited in various environments. The
        lower part of the Gadvan Formation is composed of low- energy, but not very
        deep, micritic, often argillaceous limestone with echinoids and algal fragments.
      Two sandstone units were defined in the Gadvan Formation lateral changes and
         especially discontinuity of the sandstone layers which are consist of fine clastics
        (shales and siltstones) may be expected The Gadvan formation divided to three
          part:
            Upper Gadvan
       The upper part appears with occurrence of terrigenous rock. The lithology is
       composed of grey claystone and some shale.
             Khalij Member
       The Khalij member appear with pure limestone, cream, light brown and in some
         intervals oil stain.
            Lower Gadvan
       The lower part consisting of alternating of marl, argillaceous limestone,
        limestone, claystone, sandy claystone and sandstone beds. The Marl is green
         gray, soft, sticky, slightly calcareous. The Argillaceous Limestone is gray white
        gray medium hard to soft, partly pyritic. The Limestone is white, white to light
         gray, hard. The Claystone is light gray, soft, sticky. The Sandy Claystone is light
         gray, soft, sticky, fine sand grained. The Sandstone is brown to gray, partly
        white buff, gray, friable, sorted, sub rounded, medium quartz grained, partly
        calcareous. This sandstone which occur in Zone-3 and Zone-5 are the reservoir
         of this formation and in this part is equivalent with Kushk member.
             Fahliyan Formation
        This formation is start with light gray, light green gray, soft Limestone
        interbedded with green gray, soft, sticky Marl, green gray, light gray, soft,
         Argillaceous Limestone and dark green gray, soft, sticky Clay stone beds. This
        formation at continue is consisting of buff white light gray, light brown, brown,
       medium hard, hard, densely, slightly argillaceous limestone and off white, white
         gray, medium hard chalky limestone beds.

    3. Nearby Wells

    The well AZNS-040 is located in Pad#50 and as per well geology program and pad
      location proximity wells the nearby wells are AZNS-045, AZNS-127, AZN-010 and
     AZNS-017.

      Nearby  Wells  Drilling  Challenges  and  Lesson
      Learned

       Drilling challenges and lesson learned for well AZNS-040 are extracted from DDR and
   EOWR of nearby wells.
     Furthermore, based on NBW study, the well AZNS-017 is a Kazhdumi Horizontal well
     and it’s drilling sequences are different from typical Fahliyan well in South Azadegan
       oilfield, therefore all drilling challenges and lesson learned have been correlated to
      typical Fahliyan well sequences.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 26” Hole Section

      Generally, 26” hole section is first step of drilling sequence in AZNS oilfield and it will
     be drill through Aghajari formation.
     This hole section main issue while drilling including Tight hole, Bit/stabilizer balling
     and hole deviation control.
    The best practice to drill this hole section is to commence drilling with low parameters
     and high viscous spud mud for first drilled stand in order to prevent washout around
      well location/cellar area, then increase drilling parameters to maximum gradually.
      In order to prevent Bit/Stabilizer balling, flow rate and mud properties must be in
     range.
     For preventing hole deviation, use stabilized BHA and drilling with controlled
     parameters, if hole deviate from vertical, try to decrease hole inclination by reaming
     and varying drilling parameters such as decrease WOB and increase RPM.
     Furthermore, reamer trip is essential to make hole as smooth as possible prior to run
      casing.
      In well AZNS-040 this section already drilled to 153m with 65-71 pcf Mw and 20” CSG
     has been run to TD and cemented to surface without any problem.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Bit balling in well AZNS-045 with 65 pcf Bentonite mud.
      2.  Noticeable cement losses while cementing 18-5/8” CSG with 115 pcf Sw in well
        AZNS-017.
      3.  Bit balling in well AZNS-127.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 17-1/2” Hole Section

     For typical Fahliyan vertical well in area II, this hole section drill through Gachsaran
      formation which is not high pressure in this zone.
     Based on NBW study and formation description, the main drilling issues in 17-1/2”
     hole are tight hole, calcium ion contamination, hole deviation from vertical and CMT
      loss while CSG cementing.
     While drilling through Gachsaran formation, drilling fluid must be salt saturated and
   Mw must be adjust with hole condition and in case of any indication of abnormality
      while drilling/tripping/reaming such as Hi-Trq, abnormal drag, tight hole, increase in
     calcium ion value, etc, the Mw should increase in 1 pcf increment to overcome drilling
     issues and prevent induced losses, also mud should be inhibited with Kcl or any caly
       inhibition additive to achieve better hole condition.
     For good hole condition and reasonable ROP, mud properties must be in range and
      flow rate must be as maximum acceptable rate especially while drilling with PDC Bit to
      obtain planned HIS.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Frequent Bit and Stabilizer balling in GS formation with 67-86 pcf KCL/Polymer
      mud due to bad mud properties in well AZNS-045.
      2.  Drilling fluid contamination with Ca++ in Gachsaran formation in well AZNS-045.
      3.  String stuck in GS formation in well AZNS-045 while back reaming due to bad hole
         condition with 84 pcf KCL/Polymer mud.
      4. Observed back flow after cementing 13-3/8” CSG in well AZNS-045, fix problem
           after several step apply pressure in well and hold.
      5.  Frequent tight hole and reaming due to low Mw with respect to hole condition in
        base of Aghajari formation in well AZNS-017.
      6.  Bit and Stabilizer balling due to low Mw and improper Mud properties in well
        AZNS-017. Mud must be inhibited to drill clay formation.
      7. Washing down 13-3/8” Casing and set casing off bottom (5.5m) due to bad hole
         condition in well AZNS-017.
      8.  Bill balling in well AZNS-127 in base of GS formation.
      9.  Frequent tight hole and string washout in GS formation in AZN-010 while drilling
         with 74-90 pcf Mw.

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 12-1/4” Hole Section

     For typical Fahliyan vertical well in area II, this hole section drilling starts from Asmari
      formation and will be finish to top of Fahliyan formation and pass through Sarvak,
     Kazhdumi and Gadvan reservoirs which contain H2S and Co2.
    The 9-5/8” Production Casing will be set in top of Fahliyan to isolate high pressure
     Fahliyan formation from other formation.
    The key point while drilling this hole section is to adjust proper Mw with respect to hole
      condition in order to prevent hole problems such as tight hole, wellbore stability
     problem, string stuck and induced losses.

      Also, inhibited drilling fluid system must be used to drill this hole section due to
     presence of different kind of formation, the normal inhibition additives such as PHPA,
     KCL, Glycol must be used in system with regard to formation being drilled and mud
      properties must be controlled as per program.
     Consider H2S and Co2 effect on mud while drilling through SV, KZ, GD formation and
       try to keep PH in range.
    As per NBW study, this section is challenging hole section of typical Fahliyan vertical
      well profile and tight hole, wellbore stability problems, mud contamination, string
     washout and string stuck have been recorded frequently in this hole section.
    The best practice to drill safely is to start drilling with salt saturated polymer mud and
     change add Kcl into mud before top of Pabdeh and control Mw as low as possible
      while drilling AS/Pabdeh formations and continue drilling while increase Mw in 1 pcf
     increment with CaCo3 if observed any abnormal sign while drilling/tripping such as Hi-
      Trq, abnormal drag, increase in calcium ion value, etc. Consider losses while drilling
     through SV formation.
     Furthermore, while drilling through Sarvak and Kazhdumi formations, mud inhibition
     must be in range (Glycol/Kcl). In case of any losses in AS, PD and SV formations tried
      to cure same with proper LCM while keep Mw as low as possible.
      Also, due to drilling through different H2S bearing formation in this section, consider
    H2S safety requirement.
     Nearby wells drilling issue in this section are listed as below:
      1.  Frequent Tight hole in GU formation (Lower) in well AZNS-045 due to low Mw and
         improper mud inhibition.
      2.  Drilling through AS/PD/GU with 2-6 BPH losses with 75-84 pcf Mw in well AZNS-
         045. Drilling to section TD with 0-2 BPH losses with 84-87.5 pcf Mw.
      3.  Differential String stuck in KZ formation in well AZNS-045, free same with HCL
         Acid, cut Mw from 87.5 pcf to 81 pcf.
      4. Remain cement in casing sue to increase in pressure while displacing cement
           after release top plug and no more pumping. Perform Top job in 9-5/8 annulus and
        D/Out cement inside 9-5/8” CSG.
      5.  Tight hole while trip in GS formation in well AZNS-017 which cured by gradually
         increase Mw.
      6.  Bit and Stabilizer balled-up in well AZNS-017 due to improper mud properties and
        low Mw.
      7.  Wireline Log tools held up in GS formation due to low Mw and bad mud properties
           in well AZNS-017.
      8.  Cement losses while cementing casing with 112 pcf Lead Sw (Mw 100 pcf) in GS
         formation well AZNS-017.
      9. Observed 2-12 BPH losses with 75-77 pcf WBM in Sarvak formation in well AZNS-
        017 (8-1/2” Hole, KZ-H well).
      10. Observed seepage losses 2 BPH and several string stuck while directional drilling
           in Kazhdumi formation with 78 pcf OBM in well AZNS-017 (8-1/2” Hole, KZ-H
           well).

           Drilling Challenges and Lesson Learned in 8-1/2” Hole Section

     For typical Fahliyan vertical well in zone-II, this hole section is the last section of
       drilling sequences and drill through Fahliyan formation, which is high pressure and
     high temperature and contains Co2 and H2S.

       drilling practice must be considered while drilling through Fahliyan and Mud properties
     must be in proper range. For this section, the KCL/Polymer/Limestone mud is good
     choice to drill safely and efficiently.
     Consider H2S safety requirements while drilling/completion in Fahliyan formation.
     Nearby wells drilling issues in this section are listed as below:
      2.  Drilling with 2-6 BPH seepage losses in FH FM., with 100-106 pcf Mw in well

      5. Observed seepage losses 1-3 BPH with 100-105 pcf Mw in well AZNS-127 & with

5. Sequence of Operation

    Rig Move
     Hold pre-move meeting on location. Discuss contingency plans for:
                 Safe arrangements for R/U and R/D.
                 Safe standby areas for Rig.
                 In case move have to be suspended.
                Loss of trucks in case of repair.
                Moving at night.
     Hold pre-move safety meeting. Ensure everyone understands individual responsibilities:
    Commence rigging down. The ordering of trucks will be done by rig manager.
    Commence Rig move to AZNS-40, PAD NO. 50

                 Position Rig for optimal operations.
                Mud tanks should be empty during move. Fill water tanks and keep as full as possible

     Rig up on cellar
                 Final rig up and commence operational procedure for (AZNS-40)
                 Before leaving previous location, all equipment should be checked.
     Test all manifold and surface safety valves

    Pre-spud
      Certificate
         1.  All Rig equipment is on location, properly rigged up and function-tested. Check availability
          and content of Rig equipment inspection & maintenance records according to Client and
         API standards.

      Safety Device
          1.  Test draw-works crown block saver and record results on daily drilling report; test derrick
         man escape device (Geronimo line) and record time required for test weight on daily drilling
             report; test rig intercom system, especially for Driller-Derrick Man and Driller-Mud Logger
          communication link.
          2.  Check that all rig safety equipment, e.g., fire extinguishers, eye-wash stations etc., is installed
              at the proper locations as per rig layout diagrams.
          3.  Verify that substructure is level and foundation adequate to support drilling unit during
          whole well period and that mast is centered above rotary table.
          4.  Ensure rig alignment with Top Drive System. Make sure rig tongs and rig floor hoisting
          equipment are adequate for handling 8-1/2″ drill collars. Make sure that mechanical tong
            torque gauges for drill pipe/drill collar are properly functioning and have been calibrated;
             re-calibrated as required.

          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 62 of 205053-073-9125

      Rig Equipment
         1.  Verify that the De-suspension phase and 12-1/4” phase equipment is available in Rig site.
         2.  12-1/4” Tri-cone Bit is ready to be picked up, all nozzles installed and 12-1/4″ Bit breaker
           are on the rig floor.
         3.  Make sure single-shot or multi-shot survey tools available for vertical section survey.
         4.  Make sure all solids control equipment are correctly installed and have been function-tested
          with charging pressure gauges in place where applicable. Make sure adequate screen
           inventory for the shale shakers is available in the sizes required for the well. Make sure
          water tanks are completely filled and transfer lines from water tanks to mud system are
         hooked up. Make sure all mud materials and chemicals required to drill 12-1/4″ hole section
              is on location, in sound condition and suitably stored. Make sure that De-suspension fluid
          and kill mud has been made in sufficient volume.
         5.  Make sure that all mud pumps have been fitted with new consumable parts: liners, pistons,
            valves, seats etc. Make sure that pulsation dampeners are charged with Nitrogen to the
           proper pre-charge pressure, 30% of expected standpipe pressure during drilling of the 12-
           1/4” hole section; check if sufficient Nitrogen bottles are available on location to adjust
           pulsation dampener pre-charge pressure as required. Make sure that mud pump pop-off
           valves are set at the proper pressure for the liner sizes installed and that the mud discharge
            lines from the pop-off valves to the mud tanks are properly secured. Check that all high-
           pressure hoses are properly secured with safety chains. P/T should be done to high-pressure
           surface line of circulating system.

      Wellhead & BOP
         1.  20-3/4” 3K CHH and 20-3/4”, 3K x 13-5/8”, 5K CHS. Have cover on CHS.
         2.  Record well head and annulus pressure under Client supervision.
         3.  Overall check of well head components and function same, verify all are in good working
           order under Cliet supervision.
         4.  13-5/8”, 10K BOPs and related well control equipment must be ready in Rig site and
           pressure tested on test stump and ready for N/U on well head.
         5.  Make sure proper Cup tester, plug tester and wear bushing are available in Rig site.

      Others
         1.  Make sure that adequate supply of tools and equipment for De-suspension and drilling 12-
           1/4” hole section is available.
         2.  Ensure mud logging unit is properly rigged up and equipment are calibrated and tested
           properly.
         3.  Verify that the Rig’s fuel tanks are full to meet minimum of 3 days Rig consumption
            available on site.
         4.  Make sure all waste treatment equipment available and commissioning test is ok.

          5.  Hold pre-spud meeting with relevant service Company personnel on location. Discuss
           procedures involved throughout De-suspension phase and 12-1/4″ hole section drilling,
            reporting system and critical safety operation measures.
          6.  Prepared a pre-spud checklist as per Client standard and distributed it in Rig.
          7.  Check & observe the alignment of the rig. This check will be performed in four stages; rig
             levelling, derrick verticality, derrick alignment with rotary table, rotary table alignment with
           conductor pipe. To do this pick up 3 joints of 9-3/4" DC and check the verticality of the
            derrick with well head.
          8.  Record Rotary Table-GL and Rotary Table-CHS elevation.
          9.  Mechanical facilities for mud treatment such as:
              a.  Desander, Desilter, mud cleaner, proper size of shaker–screens, hoppers, mud guns &
               mixers, should be all available on Rig and functioning properly.
             b.  All mud tanks, mud transfer lines & connection should be checked by filling them with
               water & cross wellhead circulation.
              c. Mud engineer laboratory should be equipped with a complete set of testing equipment.
             The calibration should be done under supervision of well site drilling supervisor before
                 starting the operation.
             d.  Weight indicator, rotary speed gauge, any smart drilling instrumentation, Top Drive,
               Stroke meter, pressure gauges on manifold and in the drilling console, loss / gain gauge
              and any other gauges should be checked and calibrated.
              e.  Stand pipe manifold valves & connection must be checked & pressure tested.
                 f.  All motors should be checked under load prior to start drilling
             g.  Check & control mud stock & cement stock every day & if there is any necessity to
                request mud material, cement or any drilling tool, it should be prepared & requested at
               proper time.
             h.  P/U & M/U required 5” DP, 5” HWDP and 8-1/2” DC.

       Note: Fill up following forms and send to drilling office:
        Pre-spud check list
        Location and Well Hand Over Form (Including wellhead diagram with dimensions and
                 serial numbers and visual condition)

    De-Suspend the Well

     Sequence of Operation
1. Record well head and annulus pressure. If any pressure, bleed off and make sure pressure is zero and does
    not charge again.

                                                                              Page 63 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 64 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

NOTE:
     If there is any pressure after bleed off, call town for instruction.

2. Remove well head cover. Visually check well head, 13-3/8” CSG slip and CHS ring groove, make sure all
    are in good working order.
3. N/U 13-5/8”, 10M BOPs (13-5/8”, 5M Annular preventer, 13-5/8, 10M Double Ram preventer including
    Pipe Ram and Shear/Blind Ram & 13-5/8”, 10M Single Pipe Ram preventer) and related lines. N/U bell
    nipple and flow line.

NOTE:
   N/U all BOPs component on BOP stump as Rig-less, test same and be ready for final N/U on WH.

4. Function test Accumulator unit. Function & P/T BOPs and related lines as per NIOC standard.
5. Perform WH pressure integrity test by Cup tester.

NOTE:
   Make sure proper Cup test is available at well site.
    Limit P/T to 80% of WH RWP.

6. P/U and M/U 12-1/4” TCI Bit (Bit#1, 517 w/ 3x15/32” Jet Nozzles) and D/Out BHA (Including Junk sub),
   RIH to tag top of Cement plug @ 55m.
7. D/Out Cement plug f/ 55-100m with water while sweeping well with Hi-vis pill intermittently and dump
    remained fluid in the well.

        D/Out Parameters:
                    -   Flow Rate: 400-500 GPM
                    -  RPM: 60
                    -  WOB: 5-20 Klbs

NOTE:
    Start D/Out CMT plug with 5 Jts 8-1/2” DC and add BHA components as D/Out progress.

                    -  WOB: 5-10 Klbs

       If bumping not observed while cementing proceed to CIT, otherwise consider bumping pressure
            as CIT.

    positive test with 2000 psi. POOH.

    5/8") to LDC depth, Scrap inside 7" Liner and 9-5/8" casing before Dry test, CBU, spot pill, POOH to
    Surface.

            pressure. Detailed Dry Test program will be issued in due time.

      Discussion

12-1/4" Interval will be drilled through formations of Asmari, Pabdeh, Gurpi, Ilam, Laffan, Sarvak, Kazhdumi,
Darian and Gadvan. Salt/ KCl/ Glycol/ Sulfonated Asphalt/ CaCo3/Polymer Mud is designed for drilling this
section. Shoe of 9⅝" casing will be set at 3986m in top of Fahliyan. Different rates of downhole losses, from
seepage to complete, may be experienced through this section. Tight hole leading to pipe stuck is the other risk
of drilling here.
Based on the lithology to be drilled in 12-1/4” hole section, it is necessary to utilize shale inhibitors in active
system in case of need. The primary shale inhibitor in the system is Potassium ion for cation exchange in the
clays structure, to reduce their capacity of hydration and swelling. This will be provided by KCl concentration
of ≥15 ppb, but to be added only 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh formation (due to probable losses in Asmari
formation).
Inhibition of hydratable lithology, especially in Kazhdumi, is going to be provided by existence of 15 pbb KCl
in mud system and minimum 2-3% by volume of High Temperature Cloud Point Glycol. it is recommended to
have initial sufficient concentration of KCl (along with formulated 2-3% Glycol) in the system to commence
a safe and smooth drilling through Kazhdumi formation, Since KCl of the mud is a disturbing factor for the
quality of the Gamma log, the KCl will be allowed to be depleted and not maintained in the course of onward

                                                                              Page 86 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 87 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

drilling, so that the concentration of disturbing potassium ion drops down. Glycol might play the role of primary
shale inhibitor for the intervals exposed to low-KCl mud.
To minimize the risk of polymer fermentation whilst  drilling, Oxygen Scavenger S  is formulated  at
concentration of 0.3 ppb while having routine daily treatment as well. A very commonly used type of oxygen
scavenger is a Sodium Sulphate-based product (If required). It reacts with and eliminates dissolved oxygen as
a factor of increasing fermentation rate of natural-sourced polymers and also as a potential source of metal
corrosion in mud systems.
KCl will be allowed to be depleted gradually in the course of drilling. It will be maintained only if situation
dictates. Use of 3-4 ppb Sulfonated Asphalt while drilling through Laffan formation may be helpful against the
threat of Laffan Shale hydration in case of hole dictation. This will also improve the quality of wellbore when
we are close to running casing.
NaCl (62.5 ppb) should be solved in base water to get 69.5 pcf brine. Starch HT at 5-6 ppb and PAC LV at
1.5-2 ppb will be used to control the HPHT Fluid Loss below 7 ml/30min and keep the filter cake as thin as
possible on bore hole. 1-2 ppb Xanthan Gum provides both suspension capacity for adding CaCO3-F as weight
agent to reach desired MW and required cutting carrying capacity to clean the hole. Use of Barite should be
avoided as it can damage Ilam and Sarvak reservoirs. Although the intervals of these two formations are going
to be cased with 9⅝" casing, they are subject to be perforated and their productivities are subject to be evaluated
as secondary targets after Fahliyan reservoir tested.
Based on well bore condition and stability and Glycol, as shale inhibitor is going to be mixed equivalent of 2-
3% by volume 100 m before we reach the top of Pabdeh formation. It should be a Medium-Cloud Point Glycol
with the primary function of shale inhibition for water-based muds. It can be used while drilling Pabdeh and
Laffan shales without further maintaining to let it be depleted from the system gradually.
Centrifuges and hydrocyclones should be kept running to keep Low Gravity Solids content below 7% in order
to minimize reactive solids and improve ROP.
At section TD, minimum 1.2 times of annular volume circulation should be done prior to make a wiper trip to
surface. Monitoring the shakers for being clear of cutting helps in deciding when to stop circulation.

      Solids Control Management

    Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens to minimize the increment of fine solids in
      mud system.
    There may be a requirement to dress the shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in
        order to minimize over flow of mud at the beginning of this section and to allow full dispersion of
        hydratable polymers.
    Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All efforts
       should be made to maintain the LGS content below 7%.

     Interval Key Issues

    Drill the cement inside the casing to one or two meters before 13⅜” casing shoe, then pump Hi-Vis
         pill as a sweep.

    Maintain the Yield Point in the range 15-25 lb/100ft² to ensure adequate hole cleaning. Cuttings should
      be circulated up far above the BHA prior to connections. It should also be considered to ream at each
       connection. This will minimize the potential of cuttings settling during connections, causing packing
        off and stuck pipe. Prior any trips hole should be circulated to be cleaned and at least 1.2 times of
       bottoms-up. This will prevent tight hole on the way out and bridges, fill etc. on the way back in.

    Total Hardness content in the filtrate should be controlled less than 600 mg/lit by using Soda Ash and
       Caustic Soda

     Mixing Procedure

1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Seawater 0.881 bbl/bbl

2.  Treat Drill water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

3.  Mix 5-6 ppb Starch NF and 1.5-2 ppb PAC LV at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

4.  Mix NaCl at 77 ppb

5.  Xanthan Gum at range of 1-2 ppb at rate of 1 sack per 15 min

6.  Adjust mud weight as per hole condition by adding CaCO3-Fine

Note: As it was mentioned above, KCl, Glycol and Sulfonated Asphalt are not planned to be mixed in initial
       preparation of mud. They are supposed to be added in case of hole dictation in the system as per below
       plan:

    KCl
       To be added 100 m prior to reach Pabdeh formation due to probable losses of Asmari. It will
        be mixed at initial concentration of 15 ppb, but is supposed to be maintained in range 10-15
       ppb to section TD, unless hole condition dictates otherwise.
    Glycol
        Based on hole condition can be added while drilling through Pabdeh formation and Laffan
        formation (Optional). In each of these formations, it will be mixed at initial concentration of 2-
      3% by volume without further maintaining to let it be depleted gradually, unless hole condition
          dictates otherwise.

      Properties Discussion

Mud Weight
  Mud weigh has been planned for this section to be at range of 75-87 pcf. Controlling of MW could be done
  by running hydrodyclones and centrifuges and dressing the shakers with finest mesh screens and dumping
  mud from sand trap and dilution instead.

Plastic Viscosity
   Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment,
   coupled with whole new mud dilution.

Fluid Loss
    It is recommended that HPHT Fluid Loss be maintained below 7 ml/30min during the section. This is be
  achieved by the addition of a combination of Starch NF at 5 ppb and PAC LV at 2 ppb.

Rheology

                                                                              Page 91 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 92 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

   Maintain the Yield Point in the range of 15 to 25 lb/100ft² to ensure having adequate hole cleaning, making
   adjustment with fresh mud or water as required. Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be
   provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and
   high shear-thinning characteristics which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Total Hardness
    Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with the addition
    of Soda Ash and Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity
  pH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10 using Caustic Soda. This will maximize chemicals
   performance and minimize corrosion problems.

MBT
  Measuring of the MBT is the direct indication of formation reactivity. MBT of range of below 10 is
   acceptable. Using fine screens and high speed centrifuges will help in maintaining lower values of MBT by
   discarding the fine solids and consequently minimizes the dilution rate.

Shale and Clay Inhibition
  Shale and Clay inhibition will be achieved by utilizing KCl at range of 15-25 lb/bbl and Glycol at range of
  2-3% by volume.

      Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe
  Evidences of tight hole and stuck pipe occurred in some wells while drilling this Section. Mud must be
   inhibited to avoid the reaction with the shale and proper mud weight must be controlled. The main actions
   to take in order to avoid differential sticking are tight fluid loss control, and continuous movement of pipe
  and controlling mud weight. In the event of stuck pipe, environment-friendly pipe-freeing pill can be spotted
  around the stuck area. The other candidate in this case can be using HCl 10-15%. Because of undesired side
   effect damage to metallic parts and hole wash out, using acid is only considered for highly dramatic
   situations.

Hole Cleaning
  Xanthan Gum is the base for Rheology in the KCl Polymer system. If additional Rheology is required,
   increase Xanthan Gum concentration to enhance hole cleaning. Xanthan Gum will be used to provide an
   optimized rheological profile with elevated low-shear-rate-viscosity and high shear-thinning characteristics
  which result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity.

Carbon Dioxide
   Although it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established protocol, the mud
   should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2. In case of Carbon Dioxide
   contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to remove CO2 in the form of precipitating
   Calcium Carbonate.

Hydrogen Sulphide
   Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an established protocol
   that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically H2S. If any trace of
  H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and increase pH by Caustic Soda to maintain it
   around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in this case at range of minimum 1% by volume.

Lubricity
   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This lubricant should
   be of the type of Water-Dispersible Readily Biodegradable which provides the characteristics string wet-
   ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less chance of bit and BHA balling and enhances
  ROP.

Downhole Losses

   Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight
   material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the
   well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss
   rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly
   sized material to act as bridging agents.

  CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems of losses
  and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud properties to prevent
   or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct amount and size of bridging
   material cannot be over-stressed.

   Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr.
     No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

   Losses 10-30 bbl/hr:

      Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 5-7 ppb
      Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 5-7 ppb

        If no success, then:

          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 94 of 205053-073-9125

     Pump 50 bbl LCM pill containing:
            7 ppb CaCO3-M
            7 ppb CaCO3-C
            5 ppb Mica Medium
            5 ppb Walnut Shells Fine
            5 ppb Kwik-Seal Fine
            5 ppb CaCO3-M
     Note: System is loaded gradually from low concentration to maximum mentioned ranges.

  Losses 30-100 bbl/hr:

      Load CaCO3-M in active system up to 7 ppb
      Load CaCO3-C in active system up to 7 ppb
      Load Kwik-Seal F in system up to 5 ppb

     Shaker-man should be ready for managing a part of the return flow toward the pit-
         room by-pass shakers to avoid screens get blinded and LCM get wasted.

        If no success, then:

      Stop Drilling
      Pull out string above the loss zone
      Spot 60-90 bbl pill containing:
          Pre-Hydrated Bentonite 5-10 ppb
         30 lb/bbl CaCO3-F,M
         10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal F
         10 lb/bbl Kwik-Seal M
         10 lb/bbl Walnut-Shells F
         10 lb/bbl Mica M
          Repeat the pill twice
     If LCM pill at above concentration cannot pass through the string (bit nuzzles, etc.), we need to pump
       the pill through a Mule-Shoe while following the procedure of the next state.

  Losses more than 100 bbl/hr to Total Losses:

       In the event of severe losses, Squeeze Pills, Barite or CaCO3 or Cement Plugs, Silicate Pill or Cross-
       Linking Pills should be pumped to minimize losses.

  LCM Pill Application Procedure

                                                                              Page 94 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 95 of 205 053-073-9125

   1.  After spotting LCM pill over thief zone, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes
      and monitor the annulus. After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full.
   2.   If the hole can be filled, close the BOP and squeeze 10 bbl of LCM pill into the formation without
      exceeding 200 psi.
   3.   If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
   4.   If the LCM pill failed to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot another 50 bbl
       of LCM pill.
   5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into the formation
       without exceeding 200 psi.
   6.   If a squeeze pressure develops, hold pressure for 1 hour before running the string back to bottom.

   Notes:
      All LCM pills must be thoroughly mixed and homogenized and enough viscous before
           pumping.
      Remove filter screens from the drill pipe and if necessary, remove the strainers from the
        mud pumps suction lines.

     Casing Running & Cementing

It is important that the hole is fully clean prior to running casing. Any adjustments to mud properties before
cementing will be discussed and, if necessary, made after running the casing. Make pit management plan for
dealing with returns from running and cementing casing, with contingencies or lost circulation and dealing
with spacer returns and contaminated mud.

          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 102 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

This section will be drilled at mud weight 100 to 106 pcf and Salt Saturated/ KCl/ Glycol/ Polymer/ CaCO3/
Barite* Mud system will be used. The possible risks of this section are downhole losses, flow of gas and/or oil
and tight hole which may lead to stuck pipe. Severe losses were experienced in porous layers, especially in
Fahlian formation.
Starch HT at 5-6 ppb will be used to control the API Fluid Loss below 5-3 ml/30min and keep the filter cake
as thin as possible. Differential Stuck pipes can be encountered in this section therefore it is vital to keep thin
filter cake.
Xanthan Gum is used as the base of a thixotropic Rheology to provide adequate YP and high LSRV (Low
Shear Rate Viscosity) and high-shear-thinning-viscosity which are the key factors to ensure adequate hole
cleaning.

Mud Weight
   1. Mud Density vs. Reservoir Consideration

   Density of base water will be increased by combination of Salt (75 ppb) and KCl (11 ppb) to get brine at
   density of 75.5 pcf, then for increasing the density up to 82 pcf, CaCO3-F will be utilized. Barite* is
   proposed to be used to achieve Mud weight of 100-106 pcf.
   For this purpose, at the first stage, density of the saturated brine (polymers already mixed in) is elevated to
   at least 82 pcf by adding only CaCO3-F (>60 ppb) and then, at the second stage, further weight up of the
  mud will be done by adding Barite* (e.g. 147 ppb for MW = 100 pcf). Here, it is very important to have
  CaCO3 as much as possible and Barite* as less as possible, therefore, finding out the best ratio of these
   weight agents is subject to pilot testing for having the most optimized one while not getting in trouble with
   probable problems resulted by limitations such as excessive rheology, etc.
   Although, Barite* is not reservoir friendly, use of that along with Acid-Soluble CaCO3 provides the chance
   that removing the particles of CaCO3 while acid job causes the whole filter cake formed on the wellbore
  becomes unstable and gets washed by the flow of the formation fluids during well clean-up operation.
  The same pattern can also be assumed for the mud volumes invaded into the reservoir pores; when CaCO3
   part of a pore-plugging mud is dissolved, the whole plugging volume becomes unstable and finds the chance
   of being flushed outward.
           * It is recommended to investigate if there is any alternative for the Barite to be
             mixed along mix CaCO3; for example, combination of Barite and Hematite.
             Running pilot tests is suggested.

   2. A New Technology Solution

   In the field of modern fluids there is a solution for this problem and it is using Barite with very small particle
   size of 1 micron as the only weight agent solid. Note that the diameter sizes of commercial API Barite
   particles are typically between 25 to 75 microns.
  A trade name for such a system is WARP. It is an advanced fluid technology using treated micronized
   weighting agents for drilling and completion fluids.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 103 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

                   Comparison of particle size between Barite and WARP particles

  With WARP fluids technology, friction factors are lower, up to 10% in cased hole and 25% in open hole.
  The micron-sized weighting agents also pass more efficiently through shaker screens and open-hole
   completion screens. WARP technology is non-damaging to producing formations and completion
   hardware and creates a lower dynamic and static fluid-loss with thinner filter cakes and lower breakthrough
   pressures.
         [above paragraph is taken from below website – WARP Advanced fluids technology]
          https://www.slb.com/drilling/drilling-fluids-and-well-cementing/drilling-
          fluids/nonaqueous-drilling-fluid/warp-fluids-technology
   Also see below technical documents for further information:
          https://www.slb.com/-/media/files/mi/brochure/warp-brochure
          https://www.ijsr.net/archive/v5i9/ART20161761.pdf
          http://www.drillingcontractor.org/a-fluid-situation-29689
          http://iadc.org/dcpi/dc-mayjune05/May05-sag.pdf

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
   rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics which
   result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low
   as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Water-Dispersible Lubricant
    It should be an environmentally friendly, biodegradable and non-damaging lubricant which increases the
   lubricity of the system and reduces the torque and drag, compatible with most water-based muds. It is
   formulated at range of 1-2% by volume in this interval.

Clay-based Lithology Inhibition; a matter of caring reservoir as well

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 104 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

   Potassium Chloride is used as a Clay/Shale Inhibitor where clay can be existing in limestone layered. The
   concentration required will be based on the extent of the clay but will generally vary from 3-5% by weight
   in the system. Use of KCl in reservoir mud has also the good effect of minimizing the hydration and
   consequently swelling of the clay-based lithology of the pore’s walls. This helps in less damage to the
   reservoir caused by inevitable mud invasion.

Bio-Cide
   Starch HT, PAC LV and Xanthan Gum are subject to bacterial degradation even in saturated brines,
   therefore, a biocide should be used in the system to retard this happening and extend lift-time of the said
   products.

      Solids Control Management

    Shakers to be dressed initially with proper mesh screens. There may be a requirement to dress the
        shakers with coarser screens for a number of circulations in order to minimize surface loss of mud.
    Combination of linear motion shale shakers with centrifuges proved best results. If centrifuges are
       planned to run in Barite Recovery mode (to discard drill solids but keep MW and properties in range),
            it should be noted that there is the risk discarding CaCO3. Running retort test on samples of centrifuged
         fluids gives ideas on how justifiable the plan is.
    Constant monitoring of the underflow should determine the efficiency of this equipment. All efforts
       should be made to maintain the LGS below 7%.

      Interval Key Issues

   A very important issue of this section is providing mud weight of 100 pcf to 106 pcf while having the
       concern of reservoir damaging in one side and using Barite (typically known as reservoir damaging)
        in the other side. This was discussed in above.
   Mud weight in this interval is critical for wellbore stability and successful drilling and hole condition
        will dictate the mud density.
    Cuttings should be circulated up above the BHA prior to connections. It should also be considered to
       ream at each connection. This will minimize the potential of cuttings settling during connections,
       causing packing off and stuck pipe. Prior to trips the hole should be circulated for at least 1.5 times of
        annular volume circulation should be done prior to make a wiper trip to surface. Monitoring the shakers
        for being clear of cutting helps in deciding when to stop circulation. This will prevent tight hole on the
      way out and bridges, fill etc. on the way back in.
    Maintain a contingency stock of Caustic Soda, Zinc Carbonate, Lime, Citric Acid, Barite, Hematite
       and fine and medium size of acid-soluble LCM on board.
    Total Hardness content in the filtrate should be controlled less than 600 mg/lit by using Soda Ash and
        Caustic Soda for better performance of polymers.

   Use pre-mixes to maintain system volumes and to make necessary dilutions. The pre-mixes will

     Mixing Procedure

    1.   Fill tanks with calculated amount of Drill Water 0.722 bbl/bbl

    2.  Treat Drill Water with Caustic soda and Soda Ash

    3.  Mix 5-6 ppb Starch HT, at rate of 1 sack per 7 min

    4.  Mix KCl at 11 ppb and NaCl at 75 ppb

    5.  In case of what hole dictates, Addition of pH-Buffer, Oxygen Scavenger S, Corrosion Inhibitor,
      ZnCO3, Bio-Cide is while drilling as required.

    6.  Add CaCO3-F (61ppb) to reach MW of ±82 pcf

    7.  Add Barite to reach MW of 100 pcf (in case of need to add Barite, Calculation must be done based on
       Base fluid MW of 82pcf to refuse imposition of much solid to system. Also, more Barite can be added
        to reach higher MW).

      In case of foaming use Alcohol-Based Defoamer.

      In case of excessive torque use Lubricant at range of 1-2% by volume.

      Properties Discussion

Mud Weight

────────────────────────────────────────────

  As it was discussed in above section, a very important issue of this section is providing mud weight of 100-
  106 pcf while having the concern of reservoir damaging in one side and using Barite (typically known as
   reservoir damaging) in the other side.

Rheology
   Thixotropic characteristic of the fluid is supposed to be provided by Xanthan Gum for an optimized
   rheological profile with elevated low-shear rate-viscosity and high-shear-thinning characteristics which
   result in fluid with yield point greater than plastic viscosity. Plastic viscosity should be maintained as low
   as possible by extensive use of solids control equipment, coupled with new mud dilution.

Fluid Loss
    It is recommended that the API Fluid Loss be maintained at <5-3 ml/30min. This may best be achieved by
   the addition of 6 ppb Starch HT. Offering other High-Temp Drill-In Fluid Loss controllers is welcome and
  usage is subject to be investigated.

Total Hardness
  Total hardness should be maintained below 600 mg/lit for optimum polymer performance with the addition
  of Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda.

pH and Alkalinity
  pH should be maintained in the range of 9 to 10.5 using Soda Ash and/or Caustic Soda. This will maximize
   chemicals performance and minimize corrosion problems.

      Drilling Issues

Stuck Pipe

  The main actions to take in order to avoid differential sticking are tight fluid loss control, and continuous
  movement of pipe and controlling mud weight. In the event of stuck pipe, environment-friendly pipe-freeing
   pill can be spotted around the stuck area. The other candidate in this case can be using HCl 10-15%. Because
   of undesired side effect damage to metallic parts and hole wash out, using acid is only considered for highly
   dramatic situations.

Hole Cleaning

  The driving parameter that shows the hole cleaning, are VG-meter 6 and 3 dial readings. Prior to
   connections, the cuttings should be circulated well above the bottom hole assembly to avoid packing off
   after connections. Hole should be circulated clean before starting to POOH or back reaming.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 108 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

    Parameters affecting Hole Cleaning:

    1.  Monitoring shakers to become clear of cutting is a key factor to judge if the hole is clean.

    2.  Pump as fast as possible.

    3.  Control ROP's must be considered to avoid heavy load of cuttings in annulus.

    4.  In laminar flow the hole cleaning capacity, especially at low shear rates in large diameter sections, can
       be improved by raising the low shear-rate viscosity & gels. The best indicators will be the 6 & 3 rpm
       and initial gel.

Lubricity

   In case of high torque and drag, Lubricant can be used at range of 1-2% by volume. This lubricant should
   be of the type of environment-friendly water-dispersible readily biodegradable which provides the
   characteristics of string wet-ability by reduction of surface tension. This results in less chance of bit and
  BHA balling and enhances ROP.

Hydrogen Sulphide

   Regardless that the interval has or has not the potential of emitting any gas, this is an established protocol
   that the mud should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically H2S. If any trace of
  H2S is detected, treat the mud with 1-2 ppb Zinc Carbonate and increase pH by Caustic Soda or Lime to
   maintain it around 10. Corrosion Inhibitor should be used in this case at range of minimum 1% by volume.

Carbon Dioxide

   Although it is unlikely to detect Carbon Dioxide in this section, based on an established protocol, the mud
   should be monitored continuously for any trace of gas, here specifically CO2. In case of Carbon Dioxide
   contamination, Lime should be added at 0.5-2 ppb in order to remove CO2 in the form of precipitating
   Calcium Carbonate.

Downhole Losses

   Losses/Differential sticking will be minimized/avoided by the planned use of properly sized bridging/weight
   material (and Polymer) in conjunction with appropriate drilling practices. If seepage losses are noted on the
   well no specific action will be taken but close monitoring of the loss rate is to be made. For moderate loss
   rates addition of CaCO3 50 micron and 150 micron is recommended to ensure that there is adequate correctly
   sized material to act as bridging agents.

  CaCO3 will minimize filtrate/whole mud invasion of the reservoir and reduce potential problems of losses
  and differential sticking. The fluid loss and cake quality are two of the most important mud properties to prevent
   or alleviate potential stuck pipe. Note that, the maintenance of the correct amount and size of bridging
   material cannot be over-stressed.

────────────────────────────────────────────

 Seepage losses Less than 10 bbl/hr

  No specific action will be taken, but close monitoring of the probable loss rate is made.

 Losses from 10-30 bbl/hr

   Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

   Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10 meter drilled to
      compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

     If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
     Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by 7-10 ppb CaCO3 150-300μ & 7-10 ppb CaCO3 600μ

 Losses from 30-50 bbl/hr

   Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
   Since some of the CaCO3-M will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10 meter drilled to
      compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

        If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
     Pump 40-60 bbl of pill made by
      10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300μ
      10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 μ
      10pbb Oyster Shell-F
      10pbb Oyster Shell-M

 Losses from 50-100 bbl/hr

      Load CaCO3-M (150-300 micron) in system up to 5 ppb

      Load CaCO3-C (600-100 micron) in system up to 5 ppb
      Since some of the CaCO3-M&C will be discarded over the shakers, add 100 kg per 10 meter drilled
             to compensate the separated amount on the shakers.

         If loss not cured and even tends to increase, then:
     Pump 40-60 bbl of the following pill:
              10-20 ppb CaCO3 200-300 micron
              10-20 ppb CaCO3 600 micron
              7-10 ppb of each CaCO3 1000 micron & CaCO3 2000 micron
              5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -F

          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 110 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

              5-10 pbb Oyster Shell -M

 Losses more than 100 bbl/hr

       High concentrated LCM pill of various sizes of Calcium Carbonate and Oyster Shell-F&M&C
       should be pumped and spotted and gently squeezed over the loss zone.
     Spotting Procedure
    1.  After spotting LCM pill, pull the bit above the calculated top of the pill. Wait 30 minutes and
       monitor the annulus.
    2.  After 30 minutes, attempt to fill the annulus, if not already full. If the hole can be filled, close
     BOP and squeeze 10 bbl LCM pill into formation without exceeding 200 psi.
    3.   If the hole remains stable, continue to drill ahead.
    4.  Should the LCM pill fail to reduce the losses or the hole cannot be filled, then mix and spot
        another 50 bbl of LCM pill.
    5.  Attempt to fill the annulus. If successful, close the BOP and squeeze 20 bbl of LCM pill into the
        formation without exceeding 200 psi.
    6.   If a squeeze pressure develops, hold the pressure for 1 hour before running the drill string back
        to bottom.

Notes:
   LCM pills must be thoroughly homogenised and viscous enough before being pumped.
    Pumping high-concentrated LCM pill is subject to use of open-end DP or Mule-Shoe. Use of
     PBL Sub is a good practice too.
    Remove filter screens from the drill pipe (if there is any) and if necessary, remove strainers from
        the mud pump suction lines.

     Logging, Casing Running & Cementing

It is most importance that the hole is clean prior to logging and running liner. Any adjustments to mud
properties, such as reduction of gel strength, before logging and before running liner will be discussed. Make
pit management plan for dealing with returns from running and cementing casing, with contingencies or lost
circulation and dealing with spacer returns and contaminated mud. Reduce yield point to minimum level (if
practical) prior to cement job.
