    Completion Phase

      Fluid#1: Completion Fluid
Clear, solids-free brines are the most commonly used fluids in completion and work over operations to
minimize formation damage whilst perforation job and completion phase to improve production  rate.
Completion and work over fluids are specialized fluids used during well completion operations and remedial

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 116 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

workover procedures. These fluids must control not only subsurface pressure with density, but also must
minimize formation damage during completion and workover operations. The use of fluids that cause minimal
formation damage can result in improved production. Most reservoirs are sensitive to any fluids other than
those contained in them naturally.

At the beginning, all surface pits and all involved lines need to be cleaned and flushed thoroughly, then hole is
supposed to be displaced with inhibited CaBr2 Brine at density of 105 pcf (last mud weight applied in drilling
8 ½” section), to be ready for completing the well.

Density:
   Density of this completion fluid is to be provided by readily commercial liquid Calcium Bromide with initial
   density of 14.2 ppg (= 106 pcf = 1702 kg/m3). It is used for blending clear brine, workover brine and
   completion fluids. It is supplied in 55 gal drums. Adding 1%-volume of corrosion inhibitor (with density of
   1.01±0.01 SG) into desired volume of this material results in final density of 103 pcf. Note that, when
   consulting salt tables for formulating the fluid, the inevitable drop of density due to addition of corrosion
   inhibitor should be considered.

   Quality and specifications of CaBr2 shall meet the criteria of a standard regulation to be announced and
   conformity of the product to be supplied with the regulation is subject to be confirmed through an approved
   third-party quality testing evidence. Some very common and must-meet specs of an approved sample of
   commercial Calcium Bromide are as below:

                 Identity:                       Calcium Bromide Liquid, 14.2 SG
                 Structural Formula:             Br-Ca-Br;HOH
                 Molecular Formula:              CaBr2;H20
                 Molecular Weight:                199.9
                CaBr2 %:                  52% by weight
                 Boiling Point:                  129°C (265°F)
                Bulk Density:                    ~14.2 lb/gal (1.70 - 1.73 SG) at 25°F
                 Solubility in Water:               Miscible
                Appearance and Odor:             Clear fluid, Colorless liquid with no odor
                 Turbidity:                     6 NTU maximum
                pH Value:                     7 ±1
                 Crystallization Temperature:       -12.2°C (10°F) Approx.
                 Corrosion Rate:               < 5 MPY maximum

Corrosion:
   Salt solutions are often highly corrosive. Dissolved oxygen and massive concentration of ions are the
   primary corrosive agents in sodium-, potassium-, calcium-chloride- or bromide-brine base completion
   fluids. The solubility of oxygen in these brines decreases as saturation with the salt is approached. Anyhow

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 117 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

   corrosion inhibitor at concentration of 1% by volume and oxygen scavenger (special type compatible with
   Calcium brines) at concentration of 0.5 ppb should be added in completion fluid to minimize the risk of
   corrosion.

   Appearance of some corrosion inhibitors available in market is amber in color and slightly dark (not 100%
   clear). Using these types of product may cause reading the turbidity somehow more than what recorded
   before adding it. Selecting a type of corrosion inhibitor that besides providing the expected metal protection
   characteristics causes excess value of NTU as less as possible is a point which needs to be considered.

Alkalinity:
   Corrosion is accelerated in acidic environments (pH<7) and retarded in alkaline conditions (pH >7). As the
  pH (= -log [H+]) is increased, the concentration of H⁺ will be reduced, which may slow the corrosion rate.
   Conversely, decreasing the pH increases the concentration of H⁺ ion, which increases the cathodic reaction
   and may increase the corrosion rate (acids tend to dissolve metals faster).

   Normally, pH of 9 to 10 is adequate to mitigate most corrosions. In some cases, higher pH may be required.
  High pH values (≥9) neutralize acid gases and lower the solubility of corrosion products. This value of
   alkalinity is achieved in Calcium brines by adding 1-2 ppb Lime.

Dissolved Oxygen:
   In order to eliminate the threat of dissolved oxygen as a possible source of corrosion, use of Oxygen
   Scavenger CA is formulated in completion fluid at concentration of 0.5 ppb. Oxygen Scavenger CA is a
   catalyzed Sodium-based chemical used to scavenge oxygen dissolved in Calcium Brines and also drilling
   fluids having more than 300 ppm filtrate Calcium. It lowers the risk of corrosion and extends the life of
   metallic parts including production tubing. It is a stable solid and does not deteriorate when exposed to the
   atmosphere for extended periods of time.

  Oxygen Scavengers must be added directly through the hatch from the top of suction pit, not using/running
   mixing pump and just prior to pump the fluid into the well. Although, the concentration is very little, since
   this stage is after filtering the brine, it is recommended to do a pilot test in lab to ensure turbidity remains
   in acceptable range after adding this material.

H2S Scavenger:
  Use of liquid H2S scavenger, as a preventive safety factor, is recommended to be added at concentration of
  0.5%by volume completion fluid. It should be of the type designed specifically for brine-base fluid systems
   to remove H2S.

       Mixing Procedure; Completion Fluid (based on 105 pcf using only CaBr2)

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 118 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

    1.  Make sure that all pits and lines involved with completion fluid are thoroughly cleaned, flushed
       and free of any fluid and solid.
     Make sure that at least one large pit is kept empty for transferring ready brine into after
           given time for settling. After transferring one pit to empty pit, the first one is to be
            flushed and cleaned for accommodating the brine of next ready pit, and so on to the
              last pit.
     Depends on the rig facilities and structure, mud engineer on board may find it better to
           prepare the fluids pit-by-pit.
    2.  Transfer the content of CaBr2 drums into designated pits.
      Record the number of drums poured in each tank for accurate volume in it as the base
            of calculation for adding other additives into; do not rely on pit gauge, sounding or
        mud logging sensor, but have a look on them for comparison and/or correlation if found
             useful.
    3.  Mix Corrosion Inhibitor into pits at concentration of 3.5pbb (1% by volume).
    4.  Mix Lime into pits at concentration of 0.75 ppb.
     At least one hour after finishing first pit, check its pH to see if it is ±10. If not, then
          mix another 0.5 ppb. Repeat the procedure once or twice only if required.
    5.  Mix H2S Scavenger Liquid into pits at concentration of 0.5% by Volume.
    6. Do not add Oxygen Scavenger CA at this stage as it should be added directly from the top of
        the pit, just prior to pump the fluid into the well.
    7.  Shut down all agitators and mixing pumps, and leave the mixed fluid in the pits for at least 12
       hours to let any solid particle inside (mostly insoluble Lime) settles down.
    8.  Start transferring the clear fluid of the first pit to the empty pit by means of an air-powered
       Wilden pump.
     Make sure that the suction hose of the Wilden pump is not put deep close to the bottom
            of the pit, otherwise, settled solids are sucked in.
    9.  After finishing the first pit, stop Wilden pump, wash, flush and clean the pit, use it as the empty
         pit for accommodating the fluid of second pit using the and same above method.
TSS (Total Suspended Solids) and Turbidity (NTU: Nephelomertric Turbidity Units) of a fluid are the
parameters that are used to express the extent to which the fluid is free of solids. These factors are measured
on wellsite using a HACH® Test Kit. Most of the operations, require TSS and NTU ranging up to 40. Here,
we need TSS<30 and NTU<40 for the fluid pumping in the well and both TSS and NTU less than 100 for the
returned fluid.
For the fluids we are going to work with, i.e. packer fluid and CaBr2 completion fluid, typically, there is a high
chance of getting desired low value of TSS and NTU easily, because they are made with clear liquid CaBr2,
not powder, therefore, there is no impurity in the form of solid, but the only source of solid, here, is Lime.
Solubility of Lime is very low and after addition to the brine, a small part of that is consumed to provide the
alkalinity of the fluid and the rest remains inert in the tank as an excess lime to keep pH value buffered.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
 Contract No:
                        Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 119 of 205 053-073-9125
                SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

Therefore, the main source of solid in our completion fluid is the Lime we add. This must be noted that, if we
can reach to desired alkalinity with smaller concentration of Lime, we should avoid adding more for the sake
of buffering characteristics, as it results in more solid content and consequently more settling time and more
filtration processing.

      Fluid#2: Packer Fluid

Packer Fluid, here, is suggested to be basically CaBr2 brine same as completion fluid introduced earlier.

      Fluid#3: Non-Solid Hi-Vis Pill

Generally, we prepare and use different types of Hi-Viscous pills based on the specifications of the two fluids
behind and ahead of the pills and the probable limitations applicable, e.g. the concern of di-valent/mono-valent
salts, or remarkably different densities.
If one of the two fluids is CaBr2 brine, the suggestion for the Hi-Vis pill is to make it using a batch of saturated
CaCl2 brine (86 pcf = 11.5 ppg) in which Hydroxy Ethyl Cellulose (HEC) is mixed as the viscosifier.
HEC is a modified high-molecular-weight. Non-ionic natural polymer especially suited for the viscosity of
brine. This non-fermenting polymer increases viscosity and carrying capacity of workover and completion
fluids and heavy brines.
HEC is used to viscosify single salt CaCl2 brines and all mono-valent-salt brines such as NaCl, NaBr, KCl,
etc. While mixing, it shows no tendency to form fisheyes and rapidly and smoothly get viscous without the
need for high shear mixing. The H-Vis pill made by HEC has a short lifetime and overtime the polymer may
become separated from the carrier fluid, therefore, it should be only prepared upon requirement and for the
needed volume. Routine usage of HEC is at concentration of ±2 ppb, at pH range of 7 to 9.

      Fluid#4: Non-Solid Spacer

Due to having a sensitive completion fluid, in terms of cost, density and being non-solid, use of spacer between
every two batches of different fluids to be pumped is a must. Here, the spacer is designed to be again saturated
CaCl2 brine (86 pcf = 11.5 ppg). This is heaviest cost-effective non-solid fluid which can be prepared to play
the role of a spacer on one end exposed to CaBr2 completion fluid. In the other side, since both CaBr2 and
CaCl2 are di-valent salts of the same cation (Calcium) there is no risk of forming precipitation as a result of
touching two brines of di-valent and mono-valent salts. This CaCl2 Brine spacer is simply made of 0.823
bbl/bbl fresh water in which 193 ppb of CaCl2 95% purity is solved. No any other additive needs to be used.

    9. Casing Program

        Material Selection

      Casing, Liner and Tubing Material selection for South Azadegan oilfield will be describe in the
      following.

         Corrosive Environment Analysis and Strength Check

     Based on  the  data  of  offset  wells  in  this  oilfield,  there  is a  certain degree  of
      corrosive  problems  in  the  4  layers  to  be  produced.  Corrosive  medium   is
      principally composed  of 2  parts: one  is  the  corrosive gases  like H2S and CO2
      existing in the produced  fluid; and the other  is the high salinity formation water.
     The contents of main corrosive fluids in offset wells are shown in below Table:

          1)  Corrosion in this oilfield is a result of combined action of H2S, CO2 and high
                salinity formation water. The corrosive mechanism  is complicated, and the
              corrosive rate on the casing is difficult to determine. Based on the NACE standard
            and the data from the Table, the producers result in severe corrosive environment.
            However, by the research on development conditions and technical indices, it can
            be found that although the corrosive fluid contents are high in the oilfield, the
              corrosive environment is not extremely serious as the following reasons:

          2)  In general, the temperature that cause the SSC/SCC is concentrated in the range
            from 20℃ to 30℃. The average depth of the horizontal section is 2,730m with the

                                                                                   Page 133 of 205

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 134 of 205053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

               reservoir temperature of 96℃, and tensional stress on the casing does not exist in
              the horizontal section. Therefore, the influence of SSC/SCC may not be considered
               for the casing/liner.

          3)  Based on the RMDP, the production GOR in the first development phase should
              not be higher than the initial GOR, therefore, the flowing pressure is higher than
              the bubble point pressure all the time, that is, degassing problems do not exist in
              the horizontal section and some vertical section, the H2S and CO2 have no chance
              of separation out of oil phase, and it is lack of prerequisite for casing corrosion.

          4)  Based on above all, the corrosive environment of the casing string is not severe.
           The optimal selection for the casing string can be stated briefly as follows.

          Material Selection of Casing String

             In  this  oilfield,  the  corrosion  of  production  string  obviously  occurs  in 2
             regions. One  is the region where the pressure  is above the bubble point; in
           which  degassing problems do  not  exist, and  the  corrosion environment  is
              relatively weak. Another one  is the region where the pressure  is below the
           bubble  point;  because  of  the  decline  of  pressure,  the  concentration  of
             corrosive  gas   will   increase  and   the   corrosion   is   relatively   serious.
            Considering the corrosive environment  is not  serious  in  the low water  cut
            production stage and the production practice  in  this  oilfield has proved the
          L80  is  fit  for  it, So,  the L80 should be taken  as  the  material  of  9-5/8″
             casing,  7″, 5 1/2″ and 4-1/2″  liner. In order  to prevent  the hazard of gas
            leakage  after  production  degassing  occurs,  9-5/8″  casing,  7″  and  4-1/2″
              liner should be Gas tight thread. 2) The 110S  is selected as the material of
             9-5/8″,  7″  and4-1/2″  casing  rather  than  L-80  due  to  the  high  strength
            requirement  in  Fahliyan  wells,  what’s more  the 110S  is  fit  for  sour  gas
           environment

C.  Selection of PR (Performance Requirement)

According to API Specification 6A 19th edition, performance requirements are specific and unique to the
product in the as-shipped condition. All products shall be designed to perform according to the requirements
of API 6A clauses 4 and clauses 10 while in the pressure and temperature ranges and corrosion environment.
Other requirements include load capability, cycles, and operating force or torque. There are two performance
requirement levels: PR1 and PR2. Valves operating as safety valves shall be of the PR2 performance level
and meet the requirements of Annex I in API 6A For SA wells, the guideline for PR selection is that all parts
not contacting well fluids in normal production period are PR1, all parts contacting well fluids are PR2 as
follow, Casing head housing and casing head spool assembly - PR1. Tubing head spool, tubing hanger and
X-mas tree - PR2.

11. Waste Management Program

NOTE: The provision of Waste Management Engineering and Operational Services to drill Fahliyan vertical oil
producer well in South Azadegan oilfield and detailed WM program will be issued in due time.
As per SOW, waste management in this location is Zero discharge system and general waste management plan will
be described in advance.

    Introduction

The recommended waste management method for this proposal is dewatering process for fluids, and fixation
process for the generated cuttings and solids. Bulk dewatering system comprises of Mixing Hopper, waste water
conditioning tank, pumps, hoses, jet nozzles, chemicals etc. Purpose the bulk dewatering system is to recycle all the
waste fluids and dumped WBM which are generated as a result of drilling activity at top holes in minimum time.
Dewatering is the process of removing the majority of colloidal size of solids phase in excess of used water base
drilling fluid by the addition of chemicals to coagulate and flocculate the solids in the mud thus blended chemically
enhanced fluid is pumped to centrifuge. Processed solids will be removed from the fluid and we would be received
cleaned water at the end. The separated cuttings will be disposed into the corral and cleaned water goes to storage
tank for future utilization, or dumping out of the rig site.
Without chemical enhancement or the dewatering process, the mechanical liquid solids separation capability of a
centrifuge is limited to 2-3 micron. Thus, dewatering overcomes this limitation by flocculation of the feed mud by
pre-treating chemically to increase the effective particle size of suspended solids. It is important to consider that
dewatering method focuses on separating liquid phase from solid phase, in the other words we surely need to test the
final water to make sure that it's not harmful for the environment or if it uses for new drilling fluid mixing, the
necessary parameters are suitable for this purpose.
Chemically Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) system is used to remove colloidal particles from non-emulsified fluids
such as water based drilling fluids that are too small to be removed by a decanting centrifuge. By employing
chemical techniques, the colloidal particles assume the size and mass that facilitates separation by a decanting
centrifuge.
The overall objective of a dewatering system is to process the drilling waste for:
1) Reduction of the liquid waste volume in drilling operation.
2) Recycling of the fluid to build new drilling fluid.
3) Dispose the processed waste to quarantine it from the environment.
4) Release in an environmentally safe and cost-effective manner.

     Waste Fluid Management

        Fluid handling

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
           South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                              Document Title
    Contract No:
                            Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 161 of 205    053-073-9125
                  SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

All hazardous and non-hazardous fluids will have to be chemically treated prior to recycling/disposal. For treating

such fluids, stabilization or chemical flocculation is carried out.

In order to reduce the impact of the cuttings and mud to environment, the following procedure is proposed.

1) Reduce the extent of dilution. For achieving this goal, first-rate solids control equipment should be used on the

rig.

2) Salt-contaminated cuttings should be kept separate from the top-hole (non-hazardous) cuttings.

3) Similarly salt contaminated and water based fluids should be kept separate from the fluid discharged from the

top-hole sections.

4) Excess and end-of-well salt contaminated fluid should be processed through the DEWATERING SYSTEM.

5) Stabilization and burial of the salt contaminated solids

     Chemically Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) System

Traditional methods of removing ultrafine solids from drilling fluids utilizing chemical techniques either rely upon a
batch approach or by using separate pieces of equipment to dose dilute and treat. The batch approach is inefficient,
as overdosing with expensive chemicals is possible. Also, controlling the feed conditions for centrifuge processing
is difficult. Using separate pieces of equipment to dilute, dose and treat is an improved method but has the
disadvantages of increased installation time and cost. The Chemically Enhanced Centrifugation (CEC) System
eliminates both of these problems by offering real-time fluid treatment as an integrated package. The CEC System
allows the operator to use dry-form Coagulant and Flocculants; this significantly reduces the purchase and
transportation costs when compared to liquid form chemicals. The CEC System is the culmination of over two
decades experience and offers an efficient method of colloidal particle treatment
If the dewatering system runs properly and we have an effective utilization, it can reduce disposal cost by more than
40% which is remarkable amount. Dewatering process involves:
1) Coagulation
2) Flocculation
3) Settling
4) Mechanical solids removal
As it's mentioned, in dewatering process two types of chemicals will be used:
a) Coagulant agent, such as: Poly aluminum chloride / Liquid or Powder
b) Flocculent agent, such as: Polyelectrolyte (Polymer) / Powder

        Coagulation

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
           South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                              Document Title
    Contract No:
                            Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 162 of 205    053-073-9125
                  SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

      Coagulation is the addition of chemicals to water causing colloidal particles within the Water to stick or bond
      together when contact is made. Mixing is utilized during the coagulation to provide a rapid and uniform
      dispersion of the chemicals and also increase the opportunity for particle to particle contact. Normally, the
       entire process occurs in less than one second.

        Flocculation
Flocculation generally follows coagulation and can be described as a chemical and physical bridging or
agglomeration of the coagulation particles. The flocculation process involves gently mixing the particles until
distinct, suspended flocks are formed.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
           South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                              Document Title
    Contract No:
                            Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 163 of 205    053-073-9125
                  SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

Mixing polymer is more important to consider, improper preparation of a polymer can affect the performance and
efficiency of the flocculation process, thereby drastically raising the cost of the polymer usage for the project. With
this in mind, the mixing system, although a simple process, must be designed and engineered properly and
professionally for successful operation. To reach this aim, the agitation must have sufficient force to achieve these
requirements, but have no centers of high shear which would damage the flocculant molecules. It's important to
consider that the polymers typically need about 30 minutes of aging after being blended with water to allow for
proper hydration and release of the free chains, due to this point in some plant a batch mixing system is
recommended which allows polymer aging before being utilized in the process.
Delivering the polymer to targeted waste is another important factor, adding the polymer to the waste should be
without damage to polymer chain to have proper flocculation, in the other words we do need maximum contact
between polymer and particles in the fluid.
Another considerable issue is running pilot test before starting the operation, the objective of the pilot testing is to
determine the most effective and economic dosage of the chemical for the process for a given fluid system.
Efficiency simply means the best coagulant and flocculants that we are able to have, and economics will be based on
the number of chemicals and concentration of each required in order to obtain satisfactory results.
The effectiveness of various chemicals is subjective, based on the size and stability of the flocs and clarity of the
resultant liquid. No doubt that we should run different numbers of tests to assure that there is no impact against the
environmental in the discharged fluid. The most important tests which have to be done for all treated fluid are:
Turbidity, Color, PH, Conductivity, Suspended solid, free chlorine, Sulfates. There is possibility to add some more
tests for other parameters depend upon the agreement and local regulations.

     Recovered water

There are three final destinations available for the generated water from dewatering unit:
1) Using in the new drilling fluid mixing.
2) Washing jobs around the rig.
3) Disposing into a designated area (disposal area), for this purpose, a written confirmation will be required from
environmental department of the region/state which states that there is no problem to dump the fluid into the
disposal area at all.

      Solids Control Equipment on the Rig

All the cutting which is generated from solids control equipment and dewatering centrifuge or any other source on the
rig site, will be discharged into corral area and need to be treat properly, the recommended method for this purpose is
named Fixation. Actually, Solidification and Stabilization are classified as fixation process when the main purpose is
to immobilize or isolate the contaminated solids. One of the most important and vital purpose of fixation is avoid
chloride contamination of environmental specifically aquifers. In this method the cuttings are-going to be mixed with
specific chemical(s) by a car/truck mixer and finally dumps into the disposal area. The requirements for this proposal
has been introduced and recommended in next pages.
It’s important to remember that any waste management project on drilling rig starts with solids control package, so to
be reached an acceptable waste management results, a professional solids control recommendation is required
seriously. So, the first introduction table would be solids control equipment on rig which is written in below.

               Item EQUIPMENT  Qty.        REMARKS

                    1          Shale shaker    3              With minimum 5G's

                    2            Desander    1                  12" cone x 2

                    3                Desilter    1                   4" cone x 22

                    4            Centrifuge    2              Barite recovery will be run

                    5       Mud cleaner     1           325 finer mesh screen installed

        Shale Shakers

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
           South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                              Document Title
    Contract No:
                            Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 165 of 205    053-073-9125
                  SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

The first and most important criterion in solids control system design is the removal of the maximum amount of
drilled solids at the first available opportunity with the minimum of mechanical handling. This can be achieved by
maximizing the screening area available at the flow-line. Failure to do so results in excessive and unnecessary use of
hydro-cyclones that create fines due to particle degradation in the centrifugal feed pump and the cones having low
work share efficiency with high fluid loss.

       Desander / Desilter

In Fluid Management Desander / Desilter should only be utilized for 2 to 3 circulations when there is more than 1-
2% sand or an excessively high level of L.G.S solids in the mud. Hydrocyclones were first introduced to process
125% - 150% of the circulating volumes in un-weighted mud, but due to the particle degradation in the centrifugal
feed pump, many ultrafine and colloidal solids are created and returned to the mud system. The cone underflow
should then be screened over the shale shakers.

        Centrifuges

Most important criteria in the function of centrifuges are the ability to maximize the operational process.
Centrifuges are generally installed with the ability to only process drilling fluid. On the work over rig one set of
centrifuge will be needed to control fluid density and yield point. If we have low mud weight we don't need barite
recovery system on the rig, but in the case of heavy mud barite recovery will be run under proper setting.

     Mud Cleaner

It’s a combination of one shale shaker with desander and desilter. It’ll be used for un-weighted fluids, its important
advantage is preventing of high loss which normally occurs in running desander and desilter. Selecting proper mesh
screen is a point, 325 mesh size or finer (up to 440) would be suitable for mud cleaner in most of the drilling fields.
The mentioned equipment are the common on almost all drilling rigs, but if any special device or equipment
requires during the operation (for instance: gumbo chain, super-colon or etc.), it could be ordered to be ready and
installed.

       Define a separation area for gathering all waste according to waste management
              procedure.
       Requirement of environment protection on location Sewage pit Area of the sewage
                 pit: 1500 m2
       Prior to spud mud pit and sewage pit must comply with the standard. Install
             cooling water spraying and circulating system for drilling pump and sewage
              circulating system for cleaning rig floor and equipment.
       Install BOP stack and pressure test shall be operated according to the drilling
            design to avoid blowout.
       Install oil supply lines and check whether there is any leakage.
     
    Management of environment protection on location:
       In drilling operation keep mud and sewage from overflowing. If it happens,
             clean up timely.
      Mud chemicals shall be stored according to the standard and shall not be
              scattered around well site. If mud chemicals scatter while loading or unloading,
             clean it up at once. The sack of mud chemicals shall be recovered. Do not
            dispose it on site.
      Enhance water management at well location and do not wash equipment with
             fresh water. Stop water flowing for long time. Overhead tanks shall be utilized.
       Oil management shall be carefully at the well site. No oil dirt on site, no
             dripping and leaking at oil tank and manifold system area.
       After the well is completed, reinforce the sewage pit ，solidify the disposed
         mud and have environment procedure fulfilled.
       Install fuel supply lines and keep them in good condition.
       All the drilling fluid materials shall be recovered and shall not be left at the
            well site after completion.
      The environmental protection personnel from COMPANY and operator side
               shall check and accept the well site environment according to the regulation after
              completion. Only well site environment is qualified, the well can be delivered.
       Transition Area for Hazardous Waste shall also be provided by each COMPANY in
               his allocated area,
      PPL/PEDEC shall approve each area before use as well. The transition area of
             hazardous waste shall be:
                    Paved, fenced, marked and illuminated
                   Equipped with appropriate Fire Extinguisher and other emergency
                     response equipment (e.g., Eye-Wash and Emergency Shower,
                       appropriate First Aid kits, neutralizer substances etc.).
                    In compliance with the requirements of handling, transportation and
                       storage of hazardous waste (based on usage chemical MSDS).
                    Configured to accommodate a safe physical separation of incompatible
                     waste materials (e.g., acids, and alkalis, organic materials and strong
                      oxidizing agents).
                    Capable enough to provide storage for the entire range of hazardous
                     wastes generated during the work.

                   The area shall be provided with Spill Containment and means of

                         shall be granted from PPL/PEDEC.

       Standard of utilization and discharging of wastes on location
       Conduct drilling operation according to the design, drilling mud is needed before spud.
       Sewage that cannot be recovered shall be put into the pit， do not discharge
      Make full use of waste water. Water in mud pump and water brake must be utilized by
                circulating. Water that is used to wash drill floor, shall be recovered after deposition.
           The recovery rate of waste water shall reach 85％.
       Disposed oil shall be recovered entirely. Recovery rate shall be 100％. Dumping of
             waste oil shall be prohibited.
       In drilling operation, non-chrome thinner high temperature mud system shall be used
              often if engineering is qualified.
       While drilling in special area adopt mud creation inhabitation techniques to decrease
              the waste mud creation.
       After completion, all the mud chemicals, bentonite, clays shall be recovered and shall
              not be left at the well site. Mud in purifying tank shall also be recovered after
              completion.
       In case of any flammable or noxious gas encountered, steps shall be taken at once to
              prevent kicks and blowout. Gas shall be guided into ignition equipment to burn it
            away.
       Burning material that may result in serious smog or horrible smell at the well site is not
              allowed. For cement or barite that may result in granular dust pollution, operation shall
            be performed in a closed system.
       For abandoned well, filled with cement plugs to seal the oil, gas or water formation.
       COMPANY/Generators are required to transport all generated wastes to the
                location/facilities designated, and licensed by authorities and/or approved/verified by
              the PPL/PEDEC (as appropriate).
       All wastes shall be transferred by approved Sub‐ COMPANY (which could be a 3rd
              party Sub-COMPANY of the COMPANY/Generator itself). The Waste Transporter
            and any other waste management service COMPANY shall be licensed in accordance
             with local regulations and are in compliance with such regulations. PPL/PEDEC shall
               verify and approve the Waste Transportation COMPANY by checking licenses and
               qualifications, audit and inspections, verification of human resources and received
               trainings etc.
       The transportation COMPANY shall ensure that all wastes are transported in a safe
            and responsible manner.

       Well Control

                1. Installation Requirements of BOP Stack and Control System:

         The distance between BOP control lines and relief lines shall be not less than 1m.
                   Steel Gap Bridge should be placed in such a way to protect lines from damage by
                  vehicle crossing. Sundries shall not be packed on the control line shield, on which
                welding operations are forbidden.

         The air supply shall be separated from that of driller’s console and directly
                 connected to the main air supply system, and shall be equipped with liquid/gas
                   separators. Excessive bending and pinching on air hoses are forbidden.

         Electric power to BOP control system shall be directly from the main switch of the
               power board, and controlled by independent switches.

         Accumulators shall be in good condition, charged at its rated value, and ready for
               work at any time.

           1.  Installation Requirements of Choke Lines and Kill Lines, and Relief Lines:

                a)   Beside the drilling spool, one manual and one HCR gate valves on the side of
                 chock manifold and two manual gate valves on the side of kill manifold shall be
                   equipped, and the manual gate valve close to the spool shall be always open.

               b)  The high-pressure co-flex hose shall be installed as straight as possible and fixed
                 by anchor after installation.

                c)   Relief lines (burning line and bleed line):

          No field welding is permitted on relief lines and the connecting style of relief
                       lines must be flanged.
           The arrangement of relief lines shall take wind directions, dwellings, roads, oil
                    tank areas, power lines and other facilities into consideration.
           While the two lines go in the same trend, the distance between the lines shall be
                        at least 0.3m, and the two lines shall be fixed independently.
           The outlets of bleed line connecting with choke manifold shall be in a safe area
                  which is at least 300m. The bleed line on the kill manifold side connecting with
                        drilling spool shall be prepared and connected when necessary (about 70m from
                     the wellhead).
           At every 10m~15m, turning points, and outlets, the lines shall be supported and
                     fixed by cement foundations with anchor bolts or ground anchors. Hanging
                     portions shall be supported firmly. If crossing the stumbling blocks such as
                   brooks or ponds is needed, metal bridging supports are necessary.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 183 of 205053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

           Pre-buried anchor bolts for cement foundations shall not be less than 20mm or
                     3/4" in diameter, and greater than 0.5m in length.

           2.  Pressure test value and requirements:

                a)  A pressure test shall be conducted successfully where there is no pressure
                    decline in 5 minutes for a low-pressure test and a minimum of 10 minutes for a
                    high-pressure test.

               b)   Prior to each high-pressure test, a low-pressure test with 200-300 psi shall be
                     carried out to verify sealing capability at the circumstance of low pressure and
                   avoid washing out sealing elements.

                c)  High pressure test should be to the rated working pressure of ram preventers or
                    the rated working pressure of the wellhead, whichever is the lowest, or to the
                     rating required in DRILLING ROGRAM. Variable bore rams should be initially
                    pressure tested on the largest and smallest OD pipe sizes that may be used
                   during the OPERATION. Annular preventers, with a joint of drill pipe installed,
                   should be tested to 70% of their working pressure. The high test for Kelly cocks,
                         kill lines and choke lines should be to their rated working pressures, each part in
                    the choke manifold is tested respectively to its rated working pressures, the relief
                      lines be pressure tested to no less than 1,450psi (10Mpa).

               d)  When casing cup tester is used, the above test pressure should not exceed 80%
                    of the internal yield pressure (burst pressure) of the exposed casing.

                e)  The control system of BOP shall be pressure tested to 3,000psi (21Mpa) for its
                        reliability before putting into use.

                   f)   Except that the BOP control system is tested with hydraulic oil, other well
                     control equipment shall be pressure tested by clear water.

                g)   Testing tools

           All required sizes of the plug type testers, and cup type testers should be
                      available for pressure testing purpose.

          When the cup type tester(s) is used for pressure test, the connection of the cup
                        testers has to be checked, to ensure it will stand the load during the high
                     pressures test. For surface casing, the cup tester is to be set in middle of the first
                    casing joint in the top, so the first casing connection (between wellhead and
                    casing head housing) below the well head is to be tested too while testing BOP
                  and wellhead.

           3.  Pressure test frequency:

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 184 of 205053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

                 All ram type preventers, annular BOP, valves, choke and kill lines, choke
                 manifold, Kelly valves and safety valves should be pressure tested at the following
                  frequencies:

           Prior to installation where possible.

           After installation of wellhead and BOP assembly and prior to drilling.

           After the disconnection or repair of any pressure containment seal in the BOP
                       stack, choke line, or choke manifold, but limited to the affected component.

           Prior to drilling into a confirmed or suspected high-pressure zone.

           At any time requested by the COMPANY REPRESENTATIVE.

           In any case, every one month or during the first trip after the one-month
                        interval with a maximum interval of 45 days. This frequency is not required for
                     shear rams. As a minimum, the shear rams are to be tested prior to resume
                        drilling operation after 9-5/8” casing string has been set and adequate WOC.

           4. Work Requirement of Well Control Equipment:

          With shut-in casing pressure lower than 1000psi, while snubbing with annular
                      preventer, drill tools shall have 18-deg shoulder tool joints, and the snubbing
                      velocity shall not be greater than 0.2m/s.

          After shut off the annular preventer or ram preventer, with the shut-in casing
                     pressure not greater than 2000psi, drill tools are allowed to pull up and down
                    with the velocity less than 0.2m/s, however, rotating or tool joint passing
                    through are forbidden.

          While drilling through pay zone and thereafter, BOP function (close-open) test
                      for the BOPs shall be performed regularly.

          Kill manifolds shall not be used for drilling fluid fill-in.

          The maximum allowed shut-in casing pressure shall be remarkably indicated on
                  choke manifolds.

          All gate valves of well control manifolds shall be tagged with serial numbers,
                  and be indicated with on/Off.

          In case shear rams were used, after shearing the drill pipe with shear rams,
                       retrieve the upper sheared drill pipe, lower a drill pipe joint with TIW valve
                       installed into the hole and close pipe rams on it to prevent the possibility of
                     shear ram’s failure.

           5.  Management of Well Control Equipment:

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 185 of 205053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

          Well control equipment used by the drilling crew shall be managed and operated
                 by designated personnel with clear post responsibilities.

          Well site shall have specified component storeroom and rubber element
                   storeroom with air conditioners respectively. The temperature of storerooms
                       shall meet storage requirements of components and rubber elements.

          At least 1 set is available as back-up for every type ram assembly in the well
                          site. Ram preventer side door seals and ram rubber, every type gasket and bolt
                        etc. should be enough for backup.

           6.  Killing Method and Shut-in Method:

            Driller's method is recommended for well killing.

           The hard Shut-in method is recommended for shutting in the well in Fahliyan
                        reservoir.

           7.  Well Control during drilling:

                  a)  Shut in Procedure in While on Bottom
              Position Kelly (if in use) and tool joint so that tool joints are clear of sealing
                        elements.
             Shut off pumps, check for flow.
              If flow is noted, close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled
                      choke line valve (HCR).
              If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out
                         (pipe rams vs. toll joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram locks
             Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (if possible).
             Record shut-in drill pipe and casing pressures.
             Record volume gain and mark pits.
             Weigh mud in suction pits.
             Check blowout preventer and manifold for leaks.
             Check flowline and choke exhaust for flow.
             Check accumulator pressure.

                 b)   Shut in Procedure in While Tripping
              If a flow is detected, install full opening safety valve and close same.
              Position tool joints clear of the sealing elements and close annular preventer
                     and open remote-controlled choke line valve (HCR).
             Make up grey valve (dart type inside BOP on full open safety valve). Then
                  Make up Kelly or top drive (insert a pup joint or single between safety
                        valve and top drive) and open safety valve.
             Record casing pressure.

────────────────────────────────────────────
────────────────────────────────────────────
          South Azadegan Oilfield Project

                                          Document Title
Contract No:
                       Project     P/T     Zone    Dep.       Disc.      Type    Sequence    Rev.      Page 186 of 205053-073-9125
               SAC      P      IIF40   DR     DE     PRG      0001      00

             Check blowout preventer, stack, and manifold for leaks.
             Check valves for correct position.
             Check accumulator pressure.
             Begin stripping to bottom.

                  c)   Shut in Procedure for Empty Wells
             Try to RIH with drill pipe as more as possible if hole condition permits, and
                         the drill pipe must be installed a Kelly cock or safety valve.
             Close the annular preventer and open remote-controlled choke line valve
                     (HCR).
              If the well has been closed using the annular preventer, check space out
                         (pipe rams vs. tool joint relative position) and close pipe rams and ram
                        locks
             Bleed off pressure between pipe rams and annular preventer (jf possible).
             Record casing pressure

           8.  Well Control During Running Casing:

         The well control while running casing is important and critical, best practices shall be
           followed, including but not limited to:
           Change out pipe rams to casing rams prior to running casing into hydrocarbon
                    bearing formation, if possible.
           The crossover between casing and drill pipe has to be available, and good
                      practice is to make it up with a joint of DP and keep on V-door.

           9.  Shut in Procedure During Logging:

           Cable shall be pull out of the hole immediately when overflow is found during logging.
                If pit gain exceeds the specified amount, the cable shall be cut immediately and treat the
           overflow in accordance with the shut-in procedure for empty wells. Continuing to pull
             the cable through the closed annular preventer is not recommended.

          10. Well Control During Testing:
          No difference to while DRILLING OPERATION, since either there is testing
                       string in the well (same as Shut-in procedure while on bottom), or tripping the
                        string. (Same as shut-in procedure while tripping).
           Likely there is some crude in the testing string, and precaution has to be taken
                    while circulating the crude out of hole during killing operations to ensure it is
                     properly handled without causing environmental impact.
          To minimize the formation damage, the killing fluids used shall be weighted
                     brine if possible, however in well control case when it occurs, killing well

          11. Well Control During Stimulation:
           Similar to during testing.
           For any residual or alive acid to be circulated out during killing operations,
                   measures have to be taken to treat the returned acid properly to avoid personnel
                  from getting hurt, and without causing any environmental damage.

          12. Well Control Drills:

              Drills shall be conducted only when hole conditions and other rig activities permit.
              Drills should be scheduled so that crews can practice drills while on bottom, while
             tripping in and while out of the hole. Each operating shift shall perform at least one BOP
                drill under different situations per month.

          13. Basic Requirement of Well Control:
           For 13-5/8”, 10K BOP, BOP should be schemed as follows: upper rams 5”,
                   middle rams are shear rams, lower rams is variable rams (2-7/8” to 5”). For
                      easily connecting, armored fire-resistant 10000psi and ID 4-1/16" flexible hoses
                     are recommended as kill/choke lines which connected with BOP directly.
           The BOP stack and choke manifold, kill line and choke line, HCR and manual
                     gate valves, inside BOP (including kelly cock) have to be H2S trimmed and
                     stand the working temperature from -10 degrees C (in case of doing N2 for
                DST) to the maximum up to 100 deg C (estimated highest temperature
                      condition).
           The BOP equipment shall be visually inspected, function tested, and
                      hydrostatically pressure tested during commissioning and Acceptance of
                      Drilling Unit prior to Commencement Date, then upon installation on a
                    wellhead, prior to drilling any hole section with a potential hydrocarbon bearing
                       reservoir, after breaking any BOP connection (such as after installation of an
                      additional wellhead section after running casing), and at least every 14-21 days
                    while the BOP is installed on the Well.
          CONTRACTOR shall submit the current well control procedures manual of
             CONTRACTOR to COMPANY for review and approval by COMPANY.
                    Valid IWCF Well Control Certificates (or IADC equivalent) must be held by all
                      tool pushers, Drillers (optional) at Drilling Supervisor level and Drillers and
                     Assistant Drillers at Driller level, as further specified in CONTRACTOR
                    Personnel HSE Requirements.

           The accumulator must be of sufficient capacity so that it is possible to close one
                      (1) ram and the bag, open a ram and the bag, re-close a ram and the bag and
                       retain 1200psi accumulator pressure.
           The “OPEN” and “CLOSED” operating positions of BOP activators of the
                    rams, annular, and remote actuated valves must be clearly identified on the
             BOP master control panel and remote panels, in English in addition to the
                     native language of the majority of the senior drilling crew.
           Shear-ram BOP activator must have a flap-cover to ensure only pre-meditated
                  and deliberated activation and to prevent accidental WORK.
           All lines and connections in the choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold,
                  choke and kill lines and high-pressure mud lines should be welded hard-piping
                    with weld-on FMC Weco “hammer-lug” 1502 unions (or Western equivalent,
                   such as Anson) or weld-on API flanges. The well control system should not
                     include any threaded screw-on hammer-lug unions, flanges, or other threaded
                   screw-on connections.
           All adapter or spacer spools between the wellhead and BOP must be
                   manufactured in accordance with API 6A, and must be complete with all
                     required studs, nuts, and ring gasket seals for both lower and upper
                     connections; minimum spare parts should include two (2) OEM spare studs
                   complete with nuts and two spare OEM ring gasket seals for both bottom and
                    top connections.
           There should be a wide-bore gas vent line from the “poor-boy” degasser; the
                       line and line outlet must be securely anchored, the line outlet must be a safe
                     distance from the well cellar, rig floor, choke manifold, and mud logging unit.
           Well Control Equipment Welding: All welds in the well control system must be
             NDT inspected and records maintained of all welding and weld inspections,
                     including choke and kill manifold, standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge
                    manifold, choke and kill lines.
           Well Control Rig Floor Information: The following must be posted on the rig
                      floor (in the Driller’s shack / “dog-house”): Well Shut-In Procedure, Well
                    Information Sheet (showing casing and hole sizes, depths, and such like), Kill
                    Sheet (including most recent slow circulation rate pressures, formation integrity
                      leak-off test information and MAASP, present mud weight, present drill string
                  and well volumes, and such like).
           The derrick substructure clear height (rotary table to ground level) needs to be
                  enough for fitting in above BOP configuration (including a tubing head and a
                       bell nipple). This need to be double checked in rig tender process. According to
                     the calculation of height of BOP stack, the substructure clear height is at least 9
                 m.
           In the case if drilling 6-1/8" hole becomes necessary, or using 3-1/2" drill pipe
                      for the cleanup run (including drill 7" shoe track), then taper drilling string (5"

                   double ram preventer, it would be very dangerous due to the variable ram
                       failure in frequently using.

      H2S Monitoring and Prevention Measure

     As per PPL/PEDEC SOW South Azadegan oilfield contains H2S bearing formations,
       precautions shall be taken in place especially in 12-1/4” & 8-1/2” hole section (for typical
       Fahliyan vertical well) while drilling, completion and well testing operation.
      H2S can be released any time while drilling, completion and well testing operation, therefore:
       The Rig shall be prepared for H2S (Training, procedures and protective gear).
      Make sure everyone on the Rig should be made aware of the hazard presented by H2S
             during their induction when they first arrive on the rig.
       The mud shall be treated to protect the drill pipe and the casing.
       All training program shall be recorded and reported.
       H2S emergency drill must be conducted frequently.
       Adequate sensors and alarms must be installed for the scope of monitoring the H2S
               releases.
